title.zh: 卷三百七十五 列傳第一百三十四 鄧肅 李邴 滕康 張守 富直柔 馮康國
title.en: Volume 375 Biographies 134: Deng Su, Li Bing, Teng Kang, Zhang Shou, Fu Zhirou, Feng Kangguo
title.raw: 卷三百七十五 列傳第一百三十四 鄧肅 李邴 滕康 張守 富直柔 馮康國 Volume 375 Biographies 134: Deng Su, Li Bing, Teng Kang, Zhang Shou, Fu Zhirou, Feng Kangguo

sentences.zh: 鄧肅 李邴 滕康 張守 富直柔 馮康國

translations.literal: Deng Su, Li Bing, Teng Kang, Zhang Shou, Fu Zhirou, Feng Kangguo
translations.idiomatic: Deng Su, Li Bing, Teng Kang, Zhang Shou, Fu Zhirou, and Feng Kangguo

sentences.zh: 鄧肅，字志宏，南劍沙縣人。

translations.literal: Deng Su, style name Zhihong, was a native of Shaxian in Nanjian.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Su, whose style name was Zhihong, came from Shaxian in Nanjian.

sentences.zh: 少警敏能文，美風儀，善談論。

translations.literal: In youth he was alert and clever, able at literary composition, handsome in deportment, and skilled at discourse.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was quick-witted and gifted with the pen, carried himself with grace, and spoke eloquently.

sentences.zh: 李綱見而奇之，相倡和，為忘年交。

translations.literal: Li Gang saw him and regarded him as extraordinary; they responded to each other's compositions and became friends across the difference in their ages.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Gang met him he was struck by his talent; they exchanged poems and became friends despite their age gap.

sentences.zh: 居父喪，哀毀逾禮，芝產其廬。

translations.literal: When he dwelt in mourning for his father, his grief and emaciation exceeded the ritual norm, and ganoderma sprouted at his hut.
translations.idiomatic: During his father's mourning he grieved beyond what ritual prescribed, until spirit fungus appeared beside his mourning shed.

sentences.zh: 入太學，所與遊皆天下名士。

translations.literal: He entered the Imperial Academy, and those with whom he associated were all famous men under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: At the Imperial Academy his companions were the foremost scholars of the realm.

sentences.zh: 時東南貢花石綱，肅作詩十一章，言守令搜求擾民，用事者見之，屏出學。

translations.literal: At that time the southeast presented tribute under the Flower-and-Stone Fleet; Su composed eleven poems stating that prefects and magistrates in their searches disturbed the people; those in power saw them and expelled him from the academy.
translations.idiomatic: When the southeast was burdened by the Flower-and-Stone tribute fleet, Su wrote eleven poems denouncing how local officials' searches harassed the populace; the powers that be read them and had him expelled from the academy.

sentences.zh: 欽宗嗣位，召對便殿，補承務郎，授鴻臚寺簿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Qinzong succeeded to the throne, he was summoned for audience in the Side Hall, appointed supplementary Court Gentleman for Palace Service, and granted the post of secretary at the Court for Diplomatic Relations.
translations.idiomatic: After Qinzong ascended the throne, Su was called to audience in the Side Hall, given the rank of Court Gentleman for Palace Service, and appointed recorder at the Court for Diplomatic Relations.

sentences.zh: 金人犯闕，肅被命詣敵營，留五十日而還。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens attacked the capital, Su was ordered to go to the enemy camp and remained fifty days before returning.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens besieged the capital he was sent to their camp, where he stayed fifty days before returning.

sentences.zh: 張邦昌僭位，肅義不屈，奔赴南京，擢左正言。

translations.literal: When Zhang Bangchang usurped the throne, Su, holding to righteousness, would not submit; he hastened to Nanjing and was promoted to Left Rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Bangchang seized the throne, Su refused on principle to bow to him, fled to Nanjing, and was promoted to Left Rectifier.

sentences.zh: 先是，朝廷賜金國帛一千萬，肅在其營，密覘，均與將士之數，大約不過八萬人，至是為上言之，且言：「金人不足畏，但其信賞必罰，不假文字，故人各用命。

translations.literal: Previously the court had presented ten million bolts of silk to the Jin state; while Su was in their camp he secretly observed and divided it equally among the officers and men—the total was roughly no more than eighty thousand—and now he reported this to the emperor, also saying: "The Jin are not to be feared, but they are trustworthy in rewards and certain in punishments, and do not rely on documents, so each man gives his utmost in their service.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the court had sent ten million bolts of silk to the Jin; while in their camp Su had secretly counted how it was shared among officers and soldiers—about eighty thousand men in all—and now told the emperor, adding: "The Jurchens are not what we should fear; they simply honor rewards and enforce punishments without leaning on paperwork, so every man fights for them with his whole will.

sentences.zh: 朝廷則不然，有同時立功而功又相等者，或已轉數官，或尚為布衣，輕重上下，只在吏手。

translations.literal: Our court is not so; when some have merit at the same time and the merit is equal, some have already been promoted through several ranks while others remain commoners—the weight, lightness, precedence, and subordination lie solely in the clerks' hands.
translations.idiomatic: Our court is different: men who earn equal merit in the same action may find one promoted several ranks and another still a commoner—the clerks alone decide who is rewarded lightly or heavily, early or late.

sentences.zh: 賞既不明，誰肯自勸？

translations.literal: When rewards are unclear, who will urge himself onward?
translations.idiomatic: If rewards are unclear, who will push himself to excel?

sentences.zh: 欲望專立功賞一司，使凡立功者得以自陳。

translations.literal: I wish to establish a separate office solely for merit rewards, so that all who have merit may state their case themselves.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that a single bureau be charged only with rewarding merit, so that every man who has served may present his own account.

sentences.zh: 若功狀已明而賞不行，或功同而賞有輕重先後者，並置之法。」

translations.literal: If the merit record is already clear yet reward is not given, or if merit is equal but reward has lightness, heaviness, precedence, or lateness, all shall be brought under the law."
translations.idiomatic: Where merit is clear but reward is withheld, or equal merit wins unequal treatment, let the law hold officials to account."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 朝臣受偽命者眾，肅請分三等定罪。

translations.literal: Many court officials had accepted false commands; Su requested that guilt be apportioned in three grades.
translations.idiomatic: Many courtiers had taken office under the puppet regime; Su asked that they be sentenced in three tiers of guilt.

sentences.zh: 上以肅在圍城中，知其姓名，令具奏。

translations.literal: Because the emperor knew that Su had been in the besieged city and knew their names, he ordered a full memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Su had been inside the besieged capital and knew the culprits by name, the emperor told him to submit a full list.

sentences.zh: 肅言：「 叛臣之上者，其惡有五：諸侍從而為執政者，王時雍、徐秉哲、吳開、呂好問、莫儔、李回是也；

translations.literal: Su said: "Among traitors of the highest grade there are five kinds of evil: those who were attendants and became chief ministers—Wang Shiyong, Xu Bingzhe, Wu Kai, Lü Haowen, Mo Chou, and Li Hui are such;
translations.idiomatic: Su said: "The gravest traitors fall into five classes: former attendants who became chief ministers—Wang Shiyong, Xu Bingzhe, Wu Kai, Lü Haowen, Mo Chou, and Li Hui;

sentences.zh: 諸庶官及宮觀而起為侍從者，胡思、朱宗、周懿文、盧襄、李擢、范宗尹是也；

translations.literal: those who rose from common posts and palace posts to become attendants—Hu Si, Zhu Zong, Zhou Yiwen, Lu Xiang, Li Zhuo, and Fan Zongyin are such;
translations.idiomatic: commoners and palace officers raised to attendants—Hu Si, Zhu Zong, Zhou Yiwen, Lu Xiang, Li Zhuo, and Fan Zongyin;

sentences.zh: 撰勸進文與赦書者，顏博文、王紹是也；

translations.literal: those who drafted the petition urging enthronement and the amnesty edict—Yan Bowen and Wang Shao are such;
translations.idiomatic: those who wrote the enthronement petition and amnesty—Yan Bowen and Wang Shao;

sentences.zh: 朝臣之為事務官者，私結十友講冊立邦昌之儀者是也；

translations.literal: court officials who were administrative officers and privately formed a society of ten friends to discuss the rites of enthroning Bangchang are such;
translations.idiomatic: court administrative officers who privately formed a group of ten to plan Bangchang's enthronement rites;

sentences.zh: 因張邦昌改名者，何昌言改為善言、其弟昌辰改為知辰是也。

translations.literal: those who changed their names because of Zhang Bangchang—He Changyan changed to Shanyan and his younger brother Changchen to Zhichen are such.
translations.idiomatic: those who renamed themselves for Zhang Bangchang—He Changyan became Shanyan and his brother Changchen became Zhichen.

sentences.zh: 乞置之嶺外。

translations.literal: I beg that they be placed beyond the Ling ranges.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that they be exiled beyond the southern mountains.

sentences.zh: 所謂叛臣之次者，其惡有三：諸執政、侍從、臺諫稱臣於偽庭，執政馮澥、曹輔是也，侍從者已行遣，獨李會尚為中書舍人，臺諫中有為金人根括而被杖，一以病得免者，其餘無不在偽楚之庭；

translations.literal: The so-called traitors of the second grade have three kinds of evil: chief ministers, attendants, and remonstrance officials who styled themselves subjects in the false court—chief ministers Feng Xi and Cao Fu are such; among attendants some have already been sent away, but Li Hui alone still serves as Secretariat Drafter; among remonstrance officials some were beaten for requisitioning goods for the Jin, and one escaped by feigning illness—the rest were all in the false Chu court;
translations.idiomatic: Second-rank traitors fall into three groups: chief ministers, attendants, and remonstrators who bowed to the puppet court—Feng Xi and Cao Fu among the ministers; most attendants have been dismissed, but Li Hui still holds the post of Secretariat Drafter; some remonstrators were beaten for plundering on behalf of the Jin, one claimed illness to escape—yet nearly all served in Zhang Bangchang's court;

sentences.zh: 以庶官而升擢者，不可勝數，乞委留守司按籍考之，則無有遺者；

translations.literal: those promoted from common posts are beyond counting; I beg that the office of the capital's military commissioner be entrusted to examine the registers, and then none will be missed;
translations.idiomatic: commoners promoted to office are beyond number—I ask the capital commissioner to search the registers so that none escape;

sentences.zh: 願為奉使者，黎確、李健、陳戩是也，乞於遠小處編管。

translations.literal: those who wished to serve as envoys—Li Que, Li Jian, and Chen E are such—I beg that they be placed under ward in remote small posts.
translations.idiomatic: envoys who volunteered to serve the puppet regime—Li Que, Li Jian, and Chen E—should be placed under ward in remote posts.

sentences.zh: 若夫庶官在位供職不廢者，但苟祿而已，乞赦其罪而錄其名，不復用為臺諫、侍從。」

translations.literal: As for common officials who remained in post and did not abandon their duties, they merely clung to salary; I beg to pardon their crime but record their names and never again employ them as remonstrance officials or attendants."
translations.idiomatic: As for minor officials who kept their posts and merely clung to salary, I ask to pardon them but record their names and never again appoint them as remonstrators or attendants."

sentences.zh: 上以為然。

translations.literal: The emperor deemed this correct.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 耿南仲得祠祿歸，其子延禧為郡守，肅劾：「南仲父子同惡，沮渡河之戰，遏勤王之兵，今日割三鎮，明日截兩河。

translations.literal: Geng Nanzhong received a stipend post and returned home; his son Yanxi served as prefect; Su impeached him, saying: "Father and son Nanzhong share the same evil: they thwarted the battle to cross the river, checked the armies that came to rescue the throne—today they cede the Three Circuits, tomorrow they cut off the Two Rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Nanzhong had retired on a temple stipend; his son Yanxi was a prefect. Su impeached them: "The Nanzhongs, father and son, share one guilt—they blocked the river crossing, held back relief armies, ceded the Three Circuits today and would sever the Two Rivers tomorrow.

sentences.zh: 及陛下欲進援京城，又為南仲父子所沮。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty wished to advance and relieve the capital, they were again thwarted by father and son Nanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty tried to march to relieve the capital, they blocked you again.

sentences.zh: 誤國如此，乞正典刑。」

translations.literal: Having harmed the state thus, I beg that the proper penalty be applied."
translations.idiomatic: They have harmed the realm this gravely—I ask that they face the full penalty of the law."

sentences.zh: 南仲嘗薦肅于欽宗，肅言之不恤，上嘉其直，賜五品服。

translations.literal: Nanzhong had once recommended Su to Emperor Qinzong; Su spoke without regard for that favor; the emperor praised his forthrightness and granted him fifth-rank robes.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhong had once recommended Su to Qinzong, but Su spoke without favor; the emperor admired his bluntness and granted him fifth-rank court dress.

sentences.zh: 范訥留守東京，肅言：「訥出師兩河，望風先遁，今語人曰：『留守之說有四，戰、守、降、走而已。

translations.literal: Fan Ne held the eastern capital in garrison; Su said: "Ne marched out to the Two Rivers, fled at the first sign of the enemy wind, and now tells people: 'The garrison commander's doctrine has four points: fight, hold, surrender, or flee—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ne was left to guard the eastern capital. Su said: "Ne marched into the Two Rivers and fled at the first rumor of the enemy; now he tells people, 'A garrison commander has four options: fight, hold, surrender, or run.

sentences.zh: 戰無卒，守無糧，不降則走。』

translations.literal: To fight there are no troops; to hold there is no grain; if one does not surrender, one flees.'
translations.idiomatic: No troops to fight, no grain to hold—if you won't surrender, you run.'

sentences.zh: 且漢得人傑，乃守關中，奔軍之將，豈宜與此。」

translations.literal: Moreover, the Han gained a man of heroic stature and then held Guanzhong; how can a general of a fleeing army be fit for this?"
translations.idiomatic: The Han held Guanzhong only after winning a hero—how can a general who fled at the first alarm be trusted with the eastern capital?"

sentences.zh: 訥遂罷。

translations.literal: Ne was thereupon dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Ne was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 內侍陳良弼肩輿至橫門外，開封買入內女童，肅連章論之。

translations.literal: The inner attendant Chen Liangbi came in a shoulder-carriage to outside the Horizontal Gate; Kaifeng purchased palace girls for him; Su submitted successive memorials criticizing this.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Chen Liangbi was carried in a sedan to the Horizontal Gate while Kaifeng bought palace girls for him; Su memorialized repeatedly against it.

sentences.zh: 時官吏多托故而去，肅建議削其仕版，而取其祿以給禁衛，若夫先假指揮徑徙江湖者，乞追付有司以正其罪。

translations.literal: At the time many officials and clerks used pretexts to depart; Su proposed to strike their names from the roster of office and take their salaries to supply the palace guard; as for those who earlier used false orders to move directly to the rivers and lakes, I beg that they be pursued and handed to the authorities to rectify their crime.
translations.idiomatic: Many officials were leaving on pretexts; Su proposed striking them from the rolls and using their salaries for the palace guard, and asked that those who had fled to the provinces on forged orders be pursued and punished.

sentences.zh: 因入對，言：「外夷之巧在文書簡，簡故速；

translations.literal: On entering for audience he said: "The skill of outer barbarians lies in simplicity of documents—simple and therefore swift;
translations.idiomatic: At audience he said: "Barbarian efficiency comes from brief paperwork—brief, and therefore fast;

sentences.zh: 中國之患在文書煩，煩故遲。」

translations.literal: the affliction of China lies in prolix documents—prolix and therefore slow."
translations.idiomatic: China's affliction is prolix paperwork—prolix, and therefore slow."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「正此討論，故並三省盡依祖宗法。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "It is precisely this that is under discussion; therefore the Three Departments alike shall wholly follow the ancestral laws."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "That is exactly what we are debating—so all Three Departments shall follow the ancestral statutes."

sentences.zh: 及建局討論祖宗官制，兩月不見施行，肅言：「太祖、太宗之時，法嚴而令速，事簡而官清，未嘗旁搜曲引以稽賞罰，故能以十萬精兵混一六合。

translations.literal: When a bureau was established to discuss the ancestral official system, two months passed without implementation being seen; Su said: "In the times of Taizu and Taizong, laws were strict and orders swift, affairs simple and officials clean; they never searched widely and cited circuitously to check rewards and punishments, and therefore were able with one hundred thousand elite troops to unify the six directions.
translations.idiomatic: A bureau was set up to review the ancestral bureaucracy, yet after two months nothing had been enacted. Su said: "Under Taizu and Taizong the law was strict and orders swift, business simple and officials clean; rewards and punishments were not buried in paperwork, and with a hundred thousand elite troops they unified the realm.

sentences.zh: 自時厥後，群臣無可議者，今日獻一策，明日獻一言，煩冗瑣碎，惟恐不備，此文書所以益煩，而政事所以益緩也。

translations.literal: From that time onward there was nothing the ministers could not debate; today one strategy was offered, tomorrow one remark—tedious, prolix, and minute, fearing only that something be left incomplete; this is why documents grow ever more prolix and why government affairs grow ever more slow.
translations.idiomatic: Since then ministers debate everything—one plan today, one remark tomorrow, tedious and exhaustive for fear anything be omitted—so paperwork grows heavier and government slower.

sentences.zh: 今兵戈未息，豈可揖遜進退，尚循無事之時？

translations.literal: Now arms have not ceased—how can one bow and yield in advance and retreat, still following times of no affairs?
translations.idiomatic: War has not ended—how can we still bow and defer as in peacetime?

sentences.zh: 欲乞限以旬日，期於必至，庶幾法嚴事簡，賞罰之權不至濡滯。」

translations.literal: I wish to beg that a limit of ten days be set, with expectation of certain arrival, so that perhaps laws may be strict and affairs simple and the power of reward and punishment may not become sodden and stagnant."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that a ten-day deadline be set and enforced, so that law may stay strict, business simple, and the power to reward and punish may not bog down."

sentences.zh: 肅在諫垣，遇事感激，不三月凡抗二十疏，言皆切至，上多採納。

translations.literal: While Su was in the remonstrance bureau, encountering affairs he was stirred to passion; within less than three months he submitted twenty remonstrances in all; his words were all incisive, and the emperor adopted many of them.
translations.idiomatic: In the remonstrance office Su spoke with passion; in under three months he submitted twenty memorials, each pointed and forceful, and the emperor adopted many.

sentences.zh: 會李綱罷，肅奏曰：「綱學雖正而術疏，謀雖深而機淺，固不足以副聖意。

translations.literal: When Li Gang was dismissed, Su memorialized, saying: "Gang's learning is correct but his methods loose, his plans deep but his timing shallow; he is indeed insufficient to meet the sage's intent.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Gang was dismissed, Su memorialized: "Gang's learning is sound but his methods crude, his plans bold but his timing poor—he may not fully meet Your Majesty's expectations.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下嘗顧臣曰：『李綱真以身徇國者。』

translations.literal: Yet Your Majesty once turned to me and said: 'Li Gang truly gives his body for the state.'
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Majesty once told me, 'Li Gang truly stakes his life for the realm.'

sentences.zh: 今日罷之，而責詞甚嚴，此臣所以有疑也。

translations.literal: Today he is dismissed, yet the language of reproach is very severe—this is why your subject has doubts.
translations.idiomatic: Today he is dismissed with harsh reproach—this is what troubles me.

sentences.zh: 且兩河百姓無所適從，綱措置不一月間，民兵稍集，今綱既去，兩河之民將如何哉？

translations.literal: Moreover, the people of the Two Rivers have nowhere to turn; within less than a month Gang's arrangements had drawn militia together somewhat; now that Gang is gone, what will become of the people of the Two Rivers?
translations.idiomatic: The people of the Two Rivers have nowhere to turn; in less than a month Gang had begun to rally militia—now that he is gone, what will become of them?

sentences.zh: 偽楚之臣紛紛在朝，李綱先乞逐逆臣邦昌，然後叛黨稍能正罪，今綱既去，叛臣將如何哉？

translations.literal: Officials of the false Chu throng the court; Li Gang first begged to expel the traitor Bangchang, and only then could the rebel faction be somewhat brought to proper punishment; now that Gang is gone, what will become of the traitors?
translations.idiomatic: Puppet-Chu officials still crowd the court; Li Gang first asked to expel Bangchang, and only then were traitors punished—now that he is gone, what of the traitors?

sentences.zh: 叛臣在朝，政事乖矣，兩河無兵，外夷驕矣，李綱於此，亦不可謂無一日之長。」

translations.literal: With traitors in court, government affairs are awry; with no armies in the Two Rivers, outer barbarians are arrogant; in this Li Gang also cannot be said to lack even a single day's strength."
translations.idiomatic: Traitors remain in court and government goes awry; the Two Rivers lack armies and foreigners grow bold—on these counts Li Gang cannot be said to lack even a day's merit."

sentences.zh: 執政怒，送肅吏部，罷歸居家。

translations.literal: The chief ministers were angry and sent Su to the Ministry of Personnel; he was dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers were furious, handed Su over to the Ministry of Personnel, dismissed him, and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 紹興二年，避寇福唐，以疾卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shaoxing, fleeing bandits he went to Futang and died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In 1132 he fled raiders to Futang, where illness took him.

sentences.zh: 李邴，字漢老，濟州任城縣人。

translations.literal: Li Bing, style name Hanlao, was a native of Rencheng County in Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bing, whose style name was Hanlao, came from Rencheng in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 中崇甯五年進士第，累官為起居舍人，試中書舍人。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Chongning, rose through offices to Diary Attendant, and passed the examination for Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He took the jinshi in 1106, rose to Diary Attendant, and passed the examination for Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 北方用兵，酬功第賞，日數十百，邴辭命無留難。

translations.literal: When the north was at war, rewarding merit and ranking rewards came by tens and hundreds each day; Bing drafted orders without delay or difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: During the northern campaigns rewards were issued by the tens and hundreds daily; Bing drafted the orders without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 除給事中、同修國史兼直學士院，遷翰林學士。

translations.literal: He was appointed Supervising Censor, co-compiler of the National History with concurrent duty in the Academy, and promoted to Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Supervising Censor and co-compiler of the National History with a concurrent post in the Academy, then promoted to Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 嘗與禁中曲宴，徽宗命賦詩，高麗使入貢，邴為館伴，徽宗遣中使持示，使者請傳錄以歸。

translations.literal: He once joined a private banquet in the Forbidden Precinct; Emperor Huizong ordered him to compose poetry; when Goryeo envoys came to present tribute, Bing served as host companion; Huizong sent an inner envoy to display the poems, and the envoys requested copies to take home.
translations.idiomatic: At a private palace banquet Huizong ordered him to compose verse; when Goryeo envoys arrived Bing served as their host, and Huizong sent a eunuch to show them his poems—the envoys asked for copies to carry home.

sentences.zh: 未幾，坐言者罷，提舉南京鴻慶宮。

translations.literal: Before long, because of remonstrators he was dismissed and made superintendent of the Hongqing Palace at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon remonstrators brought about his dismissal, and he was made superintendent of the Hongqing Palace at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 欽宗即位，除徽猷閣待制、知越州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Qinzong succeeded, he was appointed Awaiting Draft at the Huayou Pavilion and made prefect of Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Qinzong succeeded he was made Awaiting Draft at the Huayou Pavilion and prefect of Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 久之，再落職，提舉西京嵩山崇福宮。

translations.literal: After a long while he was again demoted and made superintendent of the Chongfu Palace on Mount Song in the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was demoted again and made superintendent of the Chongfu Palace on Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，復徽猷閣待制。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong succeeded, he was restored as Awaiting Draft at the Huayou Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong succeeded he was restored as Awaiting Draft at the Huayou Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，召為兵部侍郎兼直學士院。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was summoned as Vice Minister of War with concurrent duty in the Academy.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was summoned as Vice Minister of War with a concurrent post in the Academy.

sentences.zh: 苗傅、劉正彥迫上遜位，上顧邴草詔，邴請得御劄而後敢作。

translations.literal: Miao Fu and Liu Zhengyan forced the emperor to abdicate; the emperor turned to Bing to draft the edict; Bing requested to receive an imperial autograph letter before he dared compose it.
translations.idiomatic: When Miao Fu and Liu Zhengyan forced the emperor to abdicate, the emperor asked Bing to draft the edict; Bing insisted on receiving the emperor's own hand before he would write.

sentences.zh: 朱勝非請降詔赦，邴就都堂草之。

translations.literal: Zhu Shengfei requested an edict of amnesty; Bing drafted it at the Executive Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shengfei asked for an amnesty edict, and Bing drafted it at the Executive Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 除翰林學士。

translations.literal: He was appointed Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 初，邴見苗傅，面諭以逆順禍福之理，且密勸殿帥王元俾以禁旅擊賊，元唯唯不能用，即詣政事堂白朱勝非，適正彥及其党王世修在焉，又以大義責之，人為之危，邴不顧也。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Bing saw Miao Fu, he admonished him face to face with the principle of rebellion and loyalty and fortune and misfortune, and secretly urged the palace commander Wang Yuan to use the palace guard to strike the rebels; Yuan assented but could not act; Bing then went to the Executive Secretariat to inform Zhu Shengfei; it happened that Zhengyan and his partisan Wang Shixiu were present, and he again reproached them with the great principle; people thought him in peril, but Bing paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Bing had confronted Miao Fu with the logic of loyalty and rebellion, and secretly urged the palace commander Wang Yuan to strike the rebels with the guard; Yuan agreed but did nothing. Bing then went to the Executive Secretariat to inform Zhu Shengfei—just as Zhengyan and his partisan Wang Shixiu were there—and rebuked them on principle; others feared for his life, but Bing paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 時御史中丞鄭瑴又抗疏言睿聖皇帝不當改號，於是邴、瑴為端明殿學士、同簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: At the time the Censor-in-Chief Zheng E also submitted a remonstrance stating that the Sage Emperor should not have his title changed; thereupon Bing and E became Academicians of the Duanming Hall and co-signers of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Censor-in-Chief Zheng E had also remonstrated that the retired emperor's title must not be changed; Bing and E were then made Duanming Academicians and co-signers of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 邴與張守分草百官章奏，三奏三答，及太后手詔與復辟赦文，一日而具。

translations.literal: Bing and Zhang Shou divided the drafting of the hundred officials' memorials and responses—three submissions and three replies—as well as the empress dowager's handwritten edict and the amnesty for restoration of rule, all completed in a single day.
translations.idiomatic: Bing and Zhang Shou together drafted the officials' memorials and replies—three rounds each—the empress dowager's hand-edict, and the restoration amnesty, all in one day.

sentences.zh: 四月，拜尚書右丞，未幾，改參知政事。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; before long he was changed to Participant in Determining Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he became Right Vice Director of State Affairs; soon after he was made Participant in Determining Affairs.

sentences.zh: 上巡江甯，太后六宮往豫章，命邴為資政殿學士、權知行臺三省樞密院事。

translations.literal: When the emperor toured Jiangning, the empress dowager and the six palaces went to Yuzhang; Bing was ordered to be Academician of the Zizheng Hall and acting director of the traveling Three Departments and Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor toured Jiangning and the empress dowager and inner palaces went to Yuzhang, Bing was made Zizheng Academician with acting charge of the traveling Three Departments and Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 以與呂頤浩論不合，乞罷，遂以本職提舉杭州洞霄宮。

translations.literal: Because his views did not agree with Lü Yihao's, he begged to resign and was then made superintendent of the Dongxiao Palace at Hangzhou in his former capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Disagreeing with Lü Yihao, he asked to resign and was made superintendent of the Dongxiao Palace at Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 未閱月，起知平江府。

translations.literal: Within less than a month he was raised to administer Pingjiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month he was recalled to govern Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 會兄鄴失守越州，坐累落職。

translations.literal: It happened that his elder brother Ye lost Yuezhou; through connection he was demoted.
translations.idiomatic: When his elder brother Ye lost Yuezhou, Bing was demoted by association.

sentences.zh: 明年，即引赦復之，又升資政殿學士。

translations.literal: The next year, on the strength of an amnesty he was restored, and again promoted to Academician of the Zizheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The next year an amnesty restored him, and he was again promoted to Zizheng Academician.

sentences.zh: 紹興五年，詔問宰執方略，邴條上戰陣、守備、措畫、綏懷各五事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Shaoxing an edict asked the chief ministers for strategy; Bing itemized five matters each on battle arrays, defense preparations, planning, and pacification.
translations.idiomatic: In 1135 the court asked the chief ministers for strategy; Bing submitted five points each on campaigning, defense, planning, and pacification.

sentences.zh: 戰陣之利五，曰出輕兵、務遠略、儲將帥、責成功、重賞格，大略謂：「關陝為進取之地，淮南為保固之地。

translations.literal: The five advantages in battle arrays are: send out light troops, pursue distant strategy, store up generals, demand success, and weight reward scales; in outline he said: "Guan-Shaan is the ground for advance; Huainan is the ground for consolidation.
translations.idiomatic: Five principles for campaigning: deploy light troops, pursue long-range strategy, cultivate generals, demand results, and weight rewards. In outline he said: "Guan-Shaan is the ground for advance; Huainan for consolidation.

sentences.zh: 關陝雖利於進取，然不用師於京東以牽制其勢，則彼得一力以拒我。

translations.literal: Although Guan-Shaan is advantageous for advance, if troops are not used in Jingdong to check their momentum, the enemy can concentrate a single force to resist us.
translations.idiomatic: Guan-Shaan favors offense, but without troops in Jingdong to pin the enemy down, they can concentrate full strength against us.

sentences.zh: 今大將統兵者數人，皆所恃以為根本，萬一失利，將不可復用。

translations.literal: Today several great generals command troops, all relied on as the foundation; if they should fail once, the generals could not be used again.
translations.idiomatic: Several great generals now command our armies—the foundation of our force; one defeat might ruin them for further use.

sentences.zh: 偏裨中如牛皋、王進、楊珪、史康民皆京東土人，知地險易，可各配以部曲三五千人，或出淮陽，或出徐、泗，彼將奔命之不暇，此不動而分陝西重兵之一端也。

translations.literal: Among subordinate commanders, Niu Gao, Wang Jin, Yang Gui, and Shi Kangmin are all natives of Jingdong and know the terrain's perils and ease; each may be given three to five thousand troops of his own command, sallying from Huaiyang or from Xu and Si—the enemy will have no leisure to answer, and this is one means of dividing the enemy's heavy forces in Shaanxi without moving our main armies.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates such as Niu Gao, Wang Jin, Yang Gui, and Shi Kangmin are Jingdong natives who know the terrain; give each three to five thousand men to strike from Huaiyang or Xu-Si, and the enemy will be too busy to respond—dividing their Shaanxi armies without risking our main forces.

sentences.zh: 關陝今雖有二宣撫，其體尚輕，非遣大臣不可。

translations.literal: Although Guan-Shaan now has two pacification commissioners, their stature is still light; only by dispatching great ministers will it suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Guan-Shaan now has two pacification commissioners, but their authority is still too light—only a senior minister will do.

sentences.zh: 呂頤浩氣節高亮，李綱識量宏遠，威名素著，願擇其一而用之，必有以報陛下。」

translations.literal: Lü Yihao's integrity is lofty and bright, Li Gang's vision broad and far-reaching, and their martial renown long established; I wish that one of them be chosen and employed—there will surely be recompense to Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Lü Yihao is upright and resolute, Li Gang far-sighted and famed—choose one of them and he will repay Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 又言：「陛下即位之初，韓世忠、劉光世、張俊威名隱然為大將，今又有吳玠、岳飛者出矣。

translations.literal: He also said: "At the beginning of Your Majesty's reign, Han Shizhong, Liu Guangshi, and Zhang Jun were tacitly the great generals in martial renown; now Wu Jie and Yue Fei have also emerged.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "At Your Majesty's accession Han Shizhong, Liu Guangshi, and Zhang Jun were the great generals; now Wu Jie and Yue Fei have risen as well.

sentences.zh: 願詔大將，于所部舉智謀忠勇可以馭眾統師各兩三人，朝廷籍記。

translations.literal: I wish to order the great generals, from their commands, to recommend two or three men each of wisdom, loyalty, and courage able to command the masses and lead armies, and that the court register them.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that each great general nominate two or three wise, loyal, and brave men under his command who can lead troops, and that the court keep a register.

sentences.zh: 遇有事宜，使當一隊，毋隸大將，則諸人競奮才智，皆飛、玠之儔矣。

translations.literal: When affairs arise, let them take charge of a detachment, not subordinated to the great generals; then all will compete in exerting wisdom and talent, and all will be peers of Fei and Jie.
translations.idiomatic: When action is needed, let them command independent detachments, not subordinate to the great generals—then all will strive to excel, and we will breed more men like Yue Fei and Wu Jie.

sentences.zh: 大將爵位已崇，難相統一，自今用兵，第可授以成算，使自為戰而已，慎勿遣重臣臨之，以輕其權而分其功。

translations.literal: The great generals' ranks are already lofty and hard to unify under one another; from now in employing troops one may only grant them a completed plan and let them fight on their own; take care not to send heavy ministers to oversee them, lest their authority be lightened and their merit divided.
translations.idiomatic: The great generals' ranks are too high to command one another; hereafter give them a finished plan and let them fight on their own—do not send senior ministers to oversee them and dilute their authority and credit.

sentences.zh: 今卻敵退師之後，必論功行賞，願因此詔有司預定賞格，謂如得城邑及近上首領之類，自一命至節度使，皆差次使足相當。」

translations.literal: Now after repelling the enemy and withdrawing the army, merit must be discussed and rewards given; I wish therefore to order the offices to fix reward scales in advance—such as taking cities and presenting enemy leaders close at hand—from the lowest rank to military commissioner, all graded so that each is fully commensurate."
translations.idiomatic: After the enemy is repelled rewards must follow; I ask the offices to set reward scales in advance—for taking cities, capturing enemy leaders, and the like—from the lowest rank to military commissioner, each grade matched to its deed."

sentences.zh: 所謂守備之宜有五，曰固根本、習舟師、防他道、講遺策、列長戍，大略謂：「江、浙為今日根本，欲保守則失進取之利，欲進取則慮根本之傷。

translations.literal: The so-called five proprieties in defense preparations are: secure the foundation, drill the river navy, guard other routes, study legacy strategies, and array long garrisons; in outline he said: "Jiang and Zhe are today's foundation; if one wishes to conserve, one loses the advantage of advance; if one wishes to advance, one fears injury to the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Five principles for defense: secure the foundation, train the river navy, guard alternate routes, study past strategies, and post long garrisons. In outline he said: "Jiangsu and Zhejiang are our foundation today—to hold them is to forgo offense, yet to advance is to risk the foundation.

sentences.zh: 古之名將，內必屯田以自足，外必因糧於敵。

translations.literal: Famous generals of old inwardly must farm garrison fields to be self-sufficient, outwardly must draw grain from the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Great generals of old farmed within to sustain themselves and foraged on the enemy without.

sentences.zh: 誠能得以功名自任如祖逖者，舉淮南而付之，使自為進取，而不至虛內以事外。

translations.literal: If one can truly obtain a man who stakes his fame and merit on himself like Zu Ti, entrust all Huainan to him, let him advance on his own, and not empty the interior to serve the exterior.
translations.idiomatic: If we can find a man like Zu Ti who stakes his reputation on success, entrust Huainan to him for independent advance, and not drain the interior to feed foreign campaigns.

sentences.zh: 臣聞朝廷下福建造海船七百隻，必如期而辦，乞仿古制，建伏波、下瀨、樓船之官，以教習水戰，俾近上將佐領之，自成一軍，而專隸於朝廷。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that the court ordered Fujian to build seven hundred seagoing vessels, which will surely be completed on schedule; I beg to follow the ancient system and establish offices of Fubo, Xialai, and Lou chuan to teach river warfare, let nearby generals and assistants lead them, form them into a separate army, and have them report solely to the court.
translations.idiomatic: I hear the court has ordered Fujian to build seven hundred seagoing ships on schedule; I ask that we restore the ancient river-warfare offices—Fubo, Xialai, and tower-ship commands—to train naval fighting under nearby generals as a separate army reporting directly to the court.

sentences.zh: 無事則散之緣江州郡，緩急則聚而用之。

translations.literal: In times of no affairs disperse them among the riverine prefectures and commanderies; in urgency gather and employ them.
translations.idiomatic: In peace scatter them along the Yangzi prefectures; in crisis gather and deploy them.

sentences.zh: 臣度敵人他年入寇，懲創今日之敗，必先以一軍來自淮甸，為築室反耕之計，以綴我師。

translations.literal: Your subject estimates that when the enemy invades in future years, chastened by today's defeat, they will first send one army from the Huai region to build houses and turn the plow—a plan to tie down our armies.
translations.idiomatic: I expect that when the enemy raids again, stung by today's defeat, they will first send an army from the Huai plain to build fortifications and farm the land, pinning our forces in place.

sentences.zh: 然後由登、萊泛海窺吳、越，以出吾左，由武昌渡江窺江、池，以出吾右，一處不支則大事去矣。

translations.literal: Then from Deng and Lai they will cross the sea to spy on Wu and Yue and emerge on our left; from Wuchang they will cross the river to spy on Jiang and Chi and emerge on our right—if one place cannot be sustained, the great affair is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Then from Deng and Lai they will sail to probe Wu and Yue on our left; from Wuchang cross the river to probe Jiang and Chi on our right—if either flank fails, all is lost.

sentences.zh: 願預講左支右吾之策。

translations.literal: I wish to study in advance the strategy of supporting left and right.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that we plan in advance how to meet threats on both flanks.

sentences.zh: 夫兵之形無窮，願詔臨江守臣，凡可設奇以誤敵者，如吳人疑城之類，皆預為措畫。

translations.literal: The forms of warfare are boundless; I wish to order the river-guarding frontier officials that whatever stratagems can be set to mislead the enemy—such as the Wu people's dummy ramparts—be all planned in advance.
translations.idiomatic: War takes endless forms; I ask that river frontier officials plan in advance every stratagem to mislead the enemy, such as the Wu people's dummy ramparts.

sentences.zh: 今長江之險，綿數千里，守備非一，苟制得其要，則用力少而見功多。

translations.literal: Today the Yangzi's peril stretches several thousand li; defense is not one matter; if the system grasps the essentials, then little effort yields much effect.
translations.idiomatic: The Yangzi's defenses stretch thousands of li; if the system grasps the essentials, little effort will yield great effect.

sentences.zh: 願差次其最緊處，屯軍若干人，一將領之，聽其郡守節制，次緊稍緩處差降焉，有事則以大將兼統之。

translations.literal: I wish to grade the most critical places, garrison a certain number of troops with one general leading them, obeying the prefect's control; at places next in criticality and somewhat relaxed, reduce accordingly; when affairs arise let a great general take combined command.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the most critical points be ranked first, each garrisoned under one general answering to the local prefect; less critical points garrisoned more lightly; and in crisis a great general take overall command.

sentences.zh: 既久則諳熟風土，緩急可用，與旋發之師不侔矣。」

translations.literal: Over time they would become versed in local conditions, usable in emergencies—not comparable to troops dispatched on the spot."
translations.idiomatic: In time they would grow familiar with local conditions and be ready when needed—far more effective than troops rushed in at the last moment."

sentences.zh: 所謂措畫之方有五，曰親大閱、補禁衛、講軍制、訂使事、降敕榜，大略謂：「因秋冬之交，辟廣場，會諸將，取士卒才藝絕特者而爵賞之。

translations.literal: The so-called methods of planning number five, namely: preside over grand inspections, replenish the Palace Guard, reform the military system, regulate envoy affairs, and issue imperial proclamations—generally speaking: "At the turn of autumn and winter, open a broad field, assemble the generals, select soldiers of exceptional talent, and reward them with ranks and honors.
translations.idiomatic: His five planning proposals were: grand inspections, replenishing the Palace Guard, reforming military institutions, regulating diplomatic missions, and issuing imperial proclamations. In brief: "At the autumn-winter transition, open drill grounds, summon the generals, and ennoble soldiers of exceptional skill.

sentences.zh: 建炎以來，禁衛單寡，乃藉五軍以為重，臣常寒心。

translations.literal: Since the Jianyan era, the Palace Guard has been thin and sparse; the court has relied on the Five Armies alone for strength—I have often been alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Since Jianyan the Palace Guard has been woefully under strength, and the court has relied on the Five Armies alone—I have long found this troubling.

sentences.zh: 願擇忠實嚴重之將以為殿帥，稍補禁衛之闕，使隱然自成一軍，則其馭諸將也，若臂之使指矣。

translations.literal: I wish to select a loyal, steady general as commander of the rearguard guard, gradually fill the Palace Guard's vacancies, so that it forms an army in its own right; then in commanding the other generals it will be like the arm directing the fingers.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that a loyal and steady general be chosen as Palace Guard commander, the Guard's ranks gradually filled, until it stands as an army in its own right—then directing the other generals will be as effortless as the arm moving the fingers.

sentences.zh: 今諸郡廂禁冗占私役者，大郡二三千人，小郡亦數百人。

translations.literal: Today in the various prefectures, encumbered garrison troops privately employed as servants run to two or three thousand men in large prefectures and several hundred even in small ones.
translations.idiomatic: Today encumbered garrison troops across the prefectures are diverted to private service—two or three thousand men in large prefectures, several hundred even in small ones.

sentences.zh: 臣願講求，除郡守兵將官自禁軍給事外，餘兼從衣糧使自僦人以役。

translations.literal: I wish to investigate: except for prefectural military commanders and staff supplied from the regular army, let the rest be hired privately with funds from the Clothing and Rations Commission.
translations.idiomatic: I propose a thorough review: aside from prefectural commanders and officers drawn from the regular army, all other personnel should be hired privately with funds from the Clothing and Rations Commission.

sentences.zh: 大抵殺廂軍三分之二，而以其衣糧之數盡募禁軍。

translations.literal: In general, cut encumbered troops by two-thirds and use the full amount of their clothing and rations pay to recruit Palace Guard soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In general, cut encumbered troops by two-thirds and use every penny of their pay to recruit Palace Guard soldiers instead.

sentences.zh: 金人自用兵以來，未嘗不以和好為言，此決不可恃。

translations.literal: Since they began using troops, the Jurchens have never failed to speak of peace and friendship—this absolutely cannot be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: Since taking up arms, the Jurchens have never ceased talking of peace and friendship—this must not be trusted.

sentences.zh: 然二聖在彼，不可遂已，姑以餘力行之耳。

translations.literal: Yet the two emperors are held there; the effort cannot simply be abandoned—we may only spare what strength remains for it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the two emperors remain in captivity, so the effort cannot be abandoned outright—we can only spare what strength remains.

sentences.zh: 臣謂宜專命一官，如古所謂行人者，或止左右司領之，當遣使人，舉成法而授之，庶免臨時斟酌之勞，而朝廷得以專意治兵矣。

translations.literal: I hold that a single official should be specially appointed, like the ancient so-called "traveling envoy," or the Left and Right Sections could simply oversee it; when envoys are to be sent, established precedents should be assembled and entrusted to them, so as to spare last-minute deliberation and let the court concentrate on governing the army.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that one official should be specially charged with envoy affairs, as in antiquity's "traveling envoy," or the Left and Right Sections could oversee it; when missions are dispatched, established precedents should be handed over in advance, sparing last-minute improvisation and freeing the court to focus on the army.

sentences.zh: 劉豫僭叛，理必滅之，謂宜降敕榜，明著豫僭逆之罪，曉諭江北士民，此亦兵家所謂伐謀伐交者。」

translations.literal: Liu Yu's usurpation and rebellion—in principle he must be destroyed. I hold that an imperial proclamation should be issued, clearly setting forth Yu's crimes of usurpation and treason, and instructing the gentry and common people north of the Yangzi—this too is what strategists call "attacking plans and breaking alliances."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu's usurpation and rebellion must, in principle, be destroyed. An imperial proclamation should clearly set forth his crimes and instruct the people north of the Yangzi—this too is what strategists call attacking the enemy's plans and alliances."

sentences.zh: 所謂綏懷之略有五，曰宣德意、先振恤，通關津、選材能、務寬貸，大略謂：「山東大姓結為山砦以自保，今雖累年，勢必有未下者。

translations.literal: The so-called methods of appeasement number five, namely: proclaim the emperor's intent, provide relief first, open passes and crossings, select talent, and practice leniency—generally speaking: "Great clans of Shandong have formed mountain fortresses for self-defense; even after many years, there must still be some that have not submitted.
translations.idiomatic: His five pacification proposals were: proclaiming the emperor's intent, providing relief first, opening passes and crossings, selecting talent, and practicing leniency. In brief: "Great clans of Shandong have formed mountain fortresses for self-defense; even after many years, some surely remain unsubdued.

sentences.zh: 願募有心力之人，密往詔諭。

translations.literal: I wish to recruit persons of determination and send them secretly to proclaim and instruct.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that resolute men be recruited and sent secretly to proclaim the emperor's will.

sentences.zh: 應淮北遺民來歸者，令淮南州郡給以行由，差船津濟，量差地分人護送，毋得邀阻。

translations.literal: For remnant people from north of the Huai who come to submit, order Huainan prefectures and districts to issue travel permits, dispatch boats to ferry them, assign men according to locality to escort them, and not permit obstruction or delay.
translations.idiomatic: Refugees from north of the Huai who return should receive travel permits from Huainan prefectures, boats to ferry them across, and local escorts—none may obstruct or delay them.

sentences.zh: 有官人先次注授差遣，無官而貧乏者，令沿江州郡以官舍居之，仍量給錢米三兩月，其能自營為生乃止。

translations.literal: Those with official rank should receive appointments in order; those without office who are poor should be housed in government quarters by Yangzi-front prefectures, with money and grain supplied for two or three months, until they can provide for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Those with official rank should receive appointments in turn; those without office who are destitute should be housed in government quarters by Yangzi-front prefectures, with money and grain for two or three months until they can support themselves.

sentences.zh: 內有才智可用之人，隨宜任使，勿但縻以爵秩而已。

translations.literal: Among them, persons of talent and ability should be assigned as circumstances require—not merely held idle with titles and ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Among them, men of talent should be employed as circumstances warrant—not merely kept idle with titles and ranks.

sentences.zh: 凡諸將行師入境，敢抗拒者，固在剿戮。

translations.literal: Whenever generals lead armies into a region, those who dare resist will naturally be suppressed and slain.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever generals lead armies into enemy territory, those who resist will naturally be suppressed and slain.

sentences.zh: 其有善良、老弱之人，皆從寬貸，使之有更生之望。」

translations.literal: But the good, the old, and the weak should all receive lenient treatment, so that they may have hope of renewed life."
translations.idiomatic: But the innocent, the aged, and the weak should all receive lenient treatment, so that they may have hope of a new life."

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: There was no response.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial received no response.

sentences.zh: 邴閒居十有七年，薨於泉州，年六十二，諡文敏。

translations.literal: Bing lived in retirement for seventeen years, then died at Quanzhou at age sixty-two; his posthumous title was Wenmin.
translations.idiomatic: Bing lived in retirement for seventeen years, then died at Quanzhou at the age of sixty-two; he was posthumously titled Wenmin.

sentences.zh: 有《草堂集》一百卷。

translations.literal: He had a Collected Works from the Thatched Hall in one hundred juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left a Collected Works from the Thatched Hall in one hundred juan.

sentences.zh: 滕康，字子濟，應天府宋城人。

translations.literal: Teng Kang, styled Ziji, was a native of Songcheng in Yingtian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Teng Kang, courtesy name Ziji, was a native of Songcheng in Yingtian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 登崇甯五年進士第，又中詞學兼茂科，除秘書省正字，遷著作佐郎、尚書工部禮部員外郎、國子司業。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Chongning, also passed the Lexical Learning and Comprehensive Excellence examination, was appointed Rectifier in the Secretariat, and was promoted to Assistant Compiler, Outer Section Member of the Ministries of Works and Rites, and Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Chongning and also passed the Lexical Learning and Comprehensive Excellence examination. He was appointed Rectifier in the Secretariat, then promoted to Assistant Compiler, Outer Section Member of the Ministries of Works and Rites, and Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 靖康二年，元帥府聞康習憲章，召至濟州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingkang, the Marshal's Headquarters, hearing that Kang was versed in statutes and regulations, summoned him to Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingkang, the Marshal's Headquarters, learning that Kang was versed in statutes and regulations, summoned him to Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 康率群臣勸進，除太常少卿，使定登極禮儀。

translations.literal: Kang led the officials in urging [the prince] to ascend the throne; he was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and commissioned to fix the accession rituals.
translations.idiomatic: Kang led the officials in urging the prince to ascend the throne. He was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and charged with fixing the accession rituals.

sentences.zh: 凡告天及肆赦之文，皆康為之，辭意激切，聞者感動。

translations.literal: All proclamations to Heaven and texts for general amnesty were composed by Kang; their language was impassioned, and those who heard them were moved.
translations.idiomatic: All proclamations to Heaven and texts for general amnesty were composed by Kang; their language was impassioned, and all who heard them were moved.

sentences.zh: 除起居舍人、權給事中，進起居郎兼討論祖宗法度檢討官，試中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was appointed Diarist, Acting Submitted Memorial Censor, promoted to Diarist and Concurrent Reviewing Officer for Ancestral Statutes and Regulations, and provisionally made Middle Drafting Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Diarist and Acting Submitted Memorial Censor, then promoted to Diarist and Concurrent Reviewing Officer for Ancestral Statutes and Regulations, and provisionally made Middle Drafting Secretary.

sentences.zh: 會顯謨閣學士孟忠厚乞用父任減年遷官，康言：「忠厚，隆祐太后之侄也，太宗以來，凡母后兄弟之子無為侍從者。」

translations.literal: When Academician of the Hall for Manifest Loyalty Meng Zhonghou requested to use his father's service to reduce years for promotion in rank, Kang said: "Zhonghou is a nephew of Empress Dowager Longyou—since Taizong, no son of an empress dowager's brother has served as a palace attendant."
translations.idiomatic: When Academician of the Hall for Manifest Loyalty Meng Zhonghou requested to use his father's service to reduce years for promotion, Kang said: "Zhonghou is a nephew of Empress Dowager Longyou. Since Taizong, no son of an empress dowager's brother has served as a palace attendant."

sentences.zh: 武義大夫康義用登極恩，遷遙郡刺史，康又封還詞頭，言：「恩例遷官一等，謂于階官上進一階。

translations.literal: The Military Affairs Grandee Kang Yi used the accession grace to be promoted to distant-prefecture prefect; Kang again returned the draft edict, saying: "The grace precedent for promotion by one rank means advancing one step on the rank ladder.
translations.idiomatic: Military Affairs Grandee Kang Yi used the accession grace to be promoted to distant-prefecture prefect. Kang again returned the draft edict, saying: "The grace precedent for promotion by one rank means advancing one step on the rank ladder.

sentences.zh: 今康義得特旨轉一官，自武義大夫躐上遙郡刺史，名為遷一官，實升五等，紊法之甚也。

translations.literal: Today Kang Yi received a special edict to shift one office—from Military Affairs Grandee leaping up to distant-prefecture prefect—the name says one rank, but in reality five grades; such disorder of the law!
translations.idiomatic: Now Kang Yi received a special edict to shift one office—from Military Affairs Grandee leaping to distant-prefecture prefect. It is called one rank, but in reality five grades—a gross disorder of the law.

sentences.zh: 自古召亂之源，非外戚撓法，則內侍干政，漢、唐可鑒。」

translations.literal: Since antiquity the sources of disorder have been nothing but consort kin bending the law or inner attendants meddling in government—Han and Tang provide clear examples."
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity the sources of disorder have been consort kin bending the law or inner attendants meddling in government—Han and Tang provide clear examples."

sentences.zh: 凡再降旨，竟不肯行。

translations.literal: Twice more the edict was issued, but he steadfastly refused to execute it.
translations.idiomatic: The edict was issued twice more, but he steadfastly refused to carry it out.

sentences.zh: 後軍統制韓世忠以不能戢所部，坐贖金。

translations.literal: Rear Army Commander-in-Chief Han Shizhong, for inability to restrain his subordinates, was fined in lieu of punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Rear Army Commander-in-Chief Han Shizhong, for failing to restrain his subordinates, was fined in lieu of punishment.

sentences.zh: 康言：「世忠無赫赫功，祗緣捕盜微勞，遂亞節鉞。

translations.literal: Kang said: "Shizhong has no towering achievements—he rose to a military commission only for minor merit in catching bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Kang said: "Shizhong has no towering achievements—he rose to a military commission only for minor merit in catching bandits.

sentences.zh: 今其所部卒伍至奪禦器，逼諫臣於死地，乃止罰金，何以懲後？」

translations.literal: Now his soldiers have gone so far as to seize imperial weapons and drive remonstrating officials to their deaths, yet he is punished only with a fine—how can this deter others?"
translations.idiomatic: Now his soldiers have seized imperial weapons and driven remonstrating officials to their deaths, yet he is punished only with a fine—how will this deter others?"

sentences.zh: 詔降世忠一官。

translations.literal: An edict demoted Shizhong one rank.
translations.idiomatic: An edict demoted Shizhong one rank.

sentences.zh: 知江州陳彥文用劉光世奏，錄其守城功，遷龍圖閣待制。

translations.literal: Chen Yanwen, prefect of Jiang Prefecture, using Liu Guangshi's memorial, had his defense of the city recorded as merit and was promoted to Gentleman at Attendance in the Hall of Dragon Diagrams.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yanwen, prefect of Jiang Prefecture, using Liu Guangshi's memorial, had his defense of the city recorded as merit and was promoted to Gentleman at Attendance in the Hall of Dragon Diagrams.

sentences.zh: 康以光世所上彥文功狀前後牴牾，閣而未下。

translations.literal: Kang held that the merit report Guangshi submitted for Yanwen contradicted itself before and after, and kept it pending without issuing the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Kang held that the merit report Guangshi submitted for Yanwen contradicted itself, and kept the appointment pending without issuing the edict.

sentences.zh: 宰相力主彥文趣康行詞，康論不已，宰相銜之。

translations.literal: The chief councilor strongly supported Yanwen and pressed Kang to draft the edict; Kang argued without cease, and the chief councilor harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: The chief councilor strongly supported Yanwen and pressed Kang to draft the edict. Kang argued without cease, and the chief councilor harbored resentment.

sentences.zh: 會布衣省試卷子不合式，康以其文取之，諫官李處遯論奏，遂以集英殿修撰提舉杭州洞霄宮。

translations.literal: When a commoner's provincial examination paper did not conform to the required form yet Kang selected it for its literary merit, Remonstrance Official Li Chudun submitted a memorial of criticism, and Kang was made Compiler at the Hall for Assembling Excellence and Commissioner of the Dongxiao Palace in Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When a commoner's provincial examination paper did not conform to the required form yet Kang selected it for its literary merit, Remonstrance Official Li Chudun submitted a memorial of criticism, and Kang was made Compiler at the Hall for Assembling Excellence and Commissioner of the Dongxiao Palace in Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，移蹕錢塘，再除中書舍人，奏曰：「去歲郊禮前日食，而日官不以聞，廷臣不以告，使陛下所以應天者未至，故逆臣敢萌不軌者，無先事之戒也。

translations.literal: Before long the court moved to Qiantang; Kang was again appointed Middle Drafting Secretary and memorialized: "Last year before the suburban sacrifices there was a solar eclipse, yet the astronomers did not report it and court officials did not inform [Your Majesty], so Your Majesty's response to Heaven was incomplete—hence traitorous ministers dared entertain disloyal designs, with no warning beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the court moved to Qiantang, and Kang was again appointed Middle Drafting Secretary. He memorialized: "Last year, before the suburban sacrifices, there was a solar eclipse, yet the astronomers did not report it and court officials did not inform Your Majesty. Your Majesty's response to Heaven was therefore incomplete—hence traitorous ministers dared entertain disloyal designs, with no warning beforehand.

sentences.zh: 陛下即位，行再歲矣，側怛愛民之政徒為空言，而百姓不被其恩；

translations.literal: Your Majesty has reigned nearly two years; compassionate policies for the people remain empty words, and the common people receive no grace;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has reigned nearly two years, yet compassionate policies for the people remain empty words and the common people receive no grace;

sentences.zh: 哀痛責躬之詔不著事實，四方不以為信。

translations.literal: proclamations of grief and self-reproach do not accord with facts, and the four quarters do not find them credible.
translations.idiomatic: proclamations of grief and self-reproach do not accord with facts, and the realm does not find them credible.

sentences.zh: 忠佞並馳，而多士解體；

translations.literal: The loyal and the sycophantic compete together, and many scholars lose heart;
translations.idiomatic: The loyal and the sycophantic advance together, and many scholars lose heart;

sentences.zh: 刑賞失當，而三軍沮氣。

translations.literal: rewards and punishments are misplaced, and the three armies lose morale.
translations.idiomatic: rewards and punishments are misplaced, and the three armies lose morale.

sentences.zh: 臣願陛下取建炎初元以來所下詔書，所舉政事，熟思審度，得無一二不類臣言者乎？

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to take all edicts and administrative acts since the first year of Jianyan, reflect on them carefully—is there not one or two that match what I say?
translations.idiomatic: I ask Your Majesty to review all edicts and administrative acts since the first year of Jianyan and reflect carefully—is there not one or two that match what I say?

sentences.zh: 望參稽得失而罷行之。」

translations.literal: I hope you will consult successes and failures and revoke what should not stand."
translations.idiomatic: I hope Your Majesty will weigh successes and failures and revoke what should not stand."

sentences.zh: 上再三褒諭，稱其有諫臣風。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly praised and instructed him, calling him a remonstrating minister in the true mold.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor repeatedly praised and commended him, calling him a remonstrating minister in the true mold.

sentences.zh: 除左諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He was appointed Left Remonstrance and Regulation Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Left Remonstrance and Regulation Grandee.

sentences.zh: 旬日間，封章屢上，遂擢翰林學士。

translations.literal: Within ten days sealed memorials were submitted repeatedly, and he was promoted to Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days he submitted sealed memorials repeatedly and was promoted to Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 翌日，除端明殿學士、同簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: The next day he was appointed Academician of the Hall of Manifest Brightness and Concurrent Co-signatory of the Military Affairs Commission.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he was appointed Academician of the Hall of Manifest Brightness and Concurrent Co-signatory of the Military Affairs Commission.

sentences.zh: 建炎三年，宰相呂頤浩議幸武昌為趨陝之計，既移蹕建康，又議欲盡棄中原，徙居民于東南。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianyan, Chief Councilor Lü Yihao proposed that the emperor travel to Wuchang as part of a plan to move toward Shaanxi; after the court had moved to Jiankang, he again proposed abandoning the Central Plain entirely and resettling the people in the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianyan, Chief Councilor Lü Yihao proposed that the emperor travel to Wuchang as part of a plan to move toward Shaanxi. After the court had moved to Jiankang, he again proposed abandoning the Central Plain entirely and resettling the people in the southeast.

sentences.zh: 康力持不可，上悟而止。

translations.literal: Kang strenuously objected that this could not be done; the emperor understood and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Kang strenuously objected, and the emperor understood and abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 未幾，上請太后奉神主如江西，以參知政事李邴權知三省樞密院事，康為資政殿學士，同從衛以行。

translations.literal: Before long the emperor requested that the empress dowager convey the imperial ancestral tablets to Jiangxi, appointing Li Bing as Acting Administrator of the Three Departments and Military Affairs Commission; Kang became Academician of the Hall of Assisting Governance and accompanied the guard on the journey.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the emperor requested that the empress dowager convey the imperial ancestral tablets to Jiangxi, appointing Li Bing as Acting Administrator of the Three Departments and Military Affairs Commission. Kang became Academician of the Hall of Assisting Governance and accompanied the imperial guard on the journey.

sentences.zh: 邴辭疾，又命康權知，以劉玨為貳。

translations.literal: Bing pleaded illness, and Kang was again ordered to serve as acting administrator, with Liu Jue as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Bing pleaded illness, and Kang was again ordered to serve as acting administrator, with Liu Jue as deputy.

sentences.zh: 賜康褒詔，許綴宰執班奏事。

translations.literal: Kang was granted an encomium edict and permitted to join the chief councilors' rank in memorializing on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Kang was granted an encomium edict and permitted to join the chief councilors' rank when memorializing on affairs.

sentences.zh: 康從衛至洪州，劉光世護江不密，金人絕而渡，康等倉卒奉太后趨虔州。

translations.literal: Kang accompanied the guard to Hong Prefecture; Liu Guangshi's Yangzi defense was not tight, the Jurchens crossed by surprise, and Kang and the others hastily escorted the empress dowager toward Qian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Kang accompanied the guard to Hong Prefecture. Liu Guangshi's Yangzi defense was not tight; the Jurchens crossed by surprise, and Kang and the others hastily escorted the empress dowager toward Qian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 殿中侍御史張延壽論康與玨無憂國之心，至使太后涉險，為敵人追迫，責授康秘書少監，分司南京，永州居住。

translations.literal: Palace Diarist Zhang Yanshou memorialized that Kang and Jue lacked concern for the state, causing the empress dowager to face peril and be pursued by the enemy; Kang was demoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat, commissioner at Nanjing, residing in Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Diarist Zhang Yanshou memorialized that Kang and Jue lacked concern for the state, causing the empress dowager to face peril and be pursued by the enemy. Kang was demoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat, commissioner at Nanjing, and ordered to reside in Yong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 未幾，許自便，復左朝請大夫，提舉明道宮。

translations.literal: Before long he was permitted free movement; restored to Left Gentleman for Court Appearances and made Commissioner of the Mingdao Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was permitted free movement, restored to Left Gentleman for Court Appearances, and made Commissioner of the Mingdao Palace.

sentences.zh: 紹興二年九月卒，年四十八。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year of Shaoxing he died at age forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the second year of Shaoxing he died at the age of forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 八年，追復龍圖閣學士。

translations.literal: In the eighth year [his rank as] Academician of the Hall of Dragon Diagrams was posthumously restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year his rank as Academician of the Hall of Dragon Diagrams was posthumously restored.

sentences.zh: 有文集二十卷。

translations.literal: He had collected writings in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected writings in twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 張守，字子固，常州晉陵人。

translations.literal: Zhang Shou, style name Ziguo, was a native of Jinling in Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shou, whose style name was Ziguo, came from Jinling in Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 家貧無書，從人假借，過目輒不忘。

translations.literal: His family was poor and owned no books; he borrowed from others and never forgot what he read.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor and owned no books; he borrowed from others and never forgot what he read.

sentences.zh: 登崇寧元年進士第，中詞學兼茂科。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the first year of Chongning and also passed the Lexical Learning and Comprehensive Excellence examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the first year of Chongning and also passed the Lexical Learning and Comprehensive Excellence examination.

sentences.zh: 除詳定《九域圖志》編修官。

translations.literal: He was appointed revising compiler for the Detailed Verification of the Gazetteer of the Nine Regions.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed revising compiler for the Detailed Verification of the Gazetteer of the Nine Regions.

sentences.zh: 以省員罷，改宣德郎，擢為監察御史。

translations.literal: When the bureau was reduced he was dismissed, changed to Gentleman for Promoting Virtue, and promoted to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When the bureau was reduced he was dismissed, changed to Gentleman for Promoting Virtue, and promoted to Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱去。

translations.literal: He left office on account of mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He left office on account of mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 冬，召還，改官，賜五品服。

translations.literal: In winter he was recalled, had his office changed, and was granted fifth-rank vestments.
translations.idiomatic: In winter he was recalled, had his office changed, and was granted fifth-rank vestments.

sentences.zh: 上在維揚，粘罕將自東平歷泗、淮以窺行在，宰臣汪伯彥、黃潛善以為李成餘黨不足畏，上召百官各言所見。

translations.literal: The emperor was at Weiyang. Nianhan was about to come from Dongping via Si and Huai to spy on the mobile court. Chief ministers Wang Boyan and Huang Qianshan held that Li Cheng's remnant faction was not worth fearing. The emperor summoned all officials to state their views.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was at Weiyang. Nianhan was about to come from Dongping via Si and Huai to spy on the mobile court. Chief ministers Wang Boyan and Huang Qianshan held that Li Cheng's remnant faction was not worth fearing. The emperor summoned all officials to state their views.

sentences.zh: 葉夢得請上南巡，阻江為守，張俊亦奏敵勢方張，宜且南渡。

translations.literal: Ye Mengde asked the emperor to tour south and guard the Yangzi as a barrier. Zhang Jun also memorialized that the enemy's strength was still waxing and that the court should cross the Yangzi for the time being.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Mengde asked the emperor to tour south and guard the Yangzi as a barrier. Zhang Jun also memorialized that the enemy's strength was still waxing and that the court should cross the Yangzi for the time being.

sentences.zh: 守獨抗疏，上防淮渡江利害六事，又別疏言金人犯淮甸之路有四，宜擇四路帥守繕兵儲粟以捍禦之。

translations.literal: Shou alone submitted a remonstrating memorial presenting six points on the advantages and harms of defending the Huai versus crossing the Yangzi, and in a separate memorial stated that there were four routes by which the Jurchens might invade the Huai region and that four circuit commanders should be chosen to ready troops, store grain, and defend.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shou alone submitted a remonstrating memorial presenting six points on the advantages and harms of defending the Huai versus crossing the Yangzi. In a separate memorial he stated that there were four routes by which the Jurchens might invade the Huai region and that four circuit commanders should be chosen to ready troops, store grain, and defend.

sentences.zh: 疏再上，又請詔大臣惟以選將治兵為急，凡不急之務，付之都司、六曹。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted again, he also asked that the emperor edict great ministers to make selecting generals and administering troops their sole urgency, and to assign all non-urgent affairs to the Chief Office and the Six Ministries.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted again, he also asked that the emperor edict great ministers to make selecting generals and administering troops their sole urgency, and to assign all non-urgent affairs to the Chief Office and the Six Ministries.

sentences.zh: 二相滋不悅，遂建議遣守撫諭京城，守聞命即就道。

translations.literal: The two chief councilors grew increasingly displeased and thereupon proposed dispatching Shou to soothe and proclaim at the capital. Upon hearing the appointment Shou set out at once.
translations.idiomatic: The two chief councilors grew increasingly displeased and thereupon proposed dispatching Zhang Shou to soothe and proclaim at the capital. Upon hearing the appointment Zhang Shou set out at once.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，還，奏金人必來，願早為之圖，上惻然。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year he returned to court, memorialized that the Jurchens would surely come, and urged early preparation; the emperor was deeply moved.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year he returned to court, memorialized that the Jurchens would surely invade, and urged early preparation. The emperor was deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 除起居郎兼直學士院。

translations.literal: He was appointed Diarist and Concurrent Drafter of the Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Diarist and Concurrent Drafter of the Academy.

sentences.zh: 金人果渡淮，上幸臨安。

translations.literal: The Jurchens indeed crossed the Huai; the emperor traveled to Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens indeed crossed the Huai, and the emperor traveled to Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 苗、劉既平，詔赦百官，表奏皆守與李邴分為之。

translations.literal: After the Miao and Liu mutiny was suppressed, an edict amnestied all officials; petitions and memorials were divided between Shou and Li Bing to draft.
translations.idiomatic: After the Miao and Liu mutiny was suppressed, an edict amnestied all officials. Petitions and memorials were divided between Zhang Shou and Li Bing to draft.

sentences.zh: 守論宰相朱勝非不能思患預防，致賊猖獗，乞罷政，疏留中不出，既而勝非竟罷政。

translations.literal: Shou memorialized that Chief Councilor Zhu Shengfei had failed to think ahead about dangers and forestall them, allowing the rebels to grow rampant, and requested his removal; the memorial was kept at court and not issued, but soon Shengfei was dismissed after all.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shou memorialized that Chief Councilor Zhu Shengfei had failed to think ahead and forestall danger, allowing the rebels to grow rampant, and requested his removal. The memorial was kept at court and not issued, but Shengfei was dismissed after all.

sentences.zh: 呂頤浩初相，舉行司馬光之言，欲併合三省，詔侍從、臺諫集議。

translations.literal: When Lü Yihao first became chief councilor, he proposed implementing Sima Guang's views and merging the Three Departments into one; an edict ordered palace attendants and censorate remonstrators to assemble for discussion.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Yihao first became chief councilor, he proposed implementing Sima Guang's views and merging the Three Departments into one. An edict ordered palace attendants and censorate remonstrators to assemble for discussion.

sentences.zh: 守言光之所奏，較然可行，若更集眾，徙為紛紜。

translations.literal: Shou said that what Guang had memorialized was plainly feasible; to gather the multitude again would only create confusion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shou said that what Guang had memorialized was plainly feasible; to gather everyone again would only create confusion.

sentences.zh: 既而悉無異論，竟合三省為一。

translations.literal: Soon there was no dissenting opinion; the Three Departments were merged into one after all.
translations.idiomatic: Soon there was no dissent, and the Three Departments were merged into one.

sentences.zh: 上幸建康，呂頤浩、張浚葉議將奉上幸武昌為趨陝之計。

translations.literal: When the emperor traveled to Jiankang, Lü Yihao and Zhang Jun together planned to have the emperor go to Wuchang as part of the plan to move toward Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor traveled to Jiankang, Lü Yihao and Zhang Jun together planned to have the emperor go to Wuchang as part of a plan to move toward Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 時方拜浚為宣撫處置使，身任陝、蜀，守與諫議大夫滕康皆持不可，曰：「東南今日根本也，陛下遠適，則奸雄生窺伺之心。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Jun was being appointed Commissioner for Pacification and Disposition with responsibility for Shaanxi and Shu; Shou and Remonstrance Grandee Teng Kang both objected, saying: "The southeast is the foundation today; if Your Majesty travels far away, ambitious schemers will grow covetous.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhang Jun was being appointed Commissioner for Pacification and Disposition with responsibility for Shaanxi and Shu. Zhang Shou and Remonstrance Grandee Teng Kang both objected, saying: "The southeast is the foundation today. If Your Majesty travels far away, ambitious schemers will grow covetous.

sentences.zh: 況將士多陝西人，以蜀近關陝，可圖西歸，自為計耳，非為陛下與國家計也。」

translations.literal: Moreover most soldiers are natives of Shaanxi; because Shu is near the passes of Shaanxi they could scheme to return west—they are calculating for themselves, not for Your Majesty and the state."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover most soldiers are natives of Shaanxi. Because Shu is near the passes of Shaanxi, they could scheme to return west—they are calculating for themselves, not for Your Majesty and the state."

sentences.zh: 守又陳十害，至殿廬謂康曰：「幸蜀之事，吾曹當以死爭之。」

translations.literal: Shou also set forth ten harms; in the hall corridor he told Kang: "On the matter of traveling to Shu, we must dispute it to the death."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shou also set forth ten harms. In the hall corridor he told Kang: "On the matter of traveling to Shu, we must dispute it to the death."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕固以為難行。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I too have thought it hard to carry out."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "I too have thought it hard to carry out."

sentences.zh: 議遂寢。

translations.literal: The proposal was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was then dropped.

sentences.zh: 六月，久雨恒陰，呂頤浩、張浚皆謝罪求去，詔郎官以上言闕政。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, long rains and constant overcast; Lü Yihao and Zhang Jun both apologized and requested to leave office; an edict ordered officials above the rank of Secretariat duty officer to speak on faults in government.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, amid long rains and constant overcast, Lü Yihao and Zhang Jun both apologized and requested to leave office. An edict ordered officials above the rank of Secretariat duty officer to speak on faults in government.

sentences.zh: 初，守為副端時嘗上疏曰：「陛下處宮室之安，則思二帝、母后穹廬毳幕之居；

translations.literal: Earlier, when Shou was deputy director of the censorate he had submitted a memorial saying: "When Your Majesty dwells in the security of the palace, then think of the two emperors and empress dowager dwelling in felt tents and coarse shelters;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zhang Shou was deputy director of the censorate, he had submitted a memorial saying: "When Your Majesty dwells in the security of the palace, think of the two emperors and empress dowager dwelling in felt tents and coarse shelters;

sentences.zh: 享膳羞之奉，則思二帝、母后膻肉酪漿之味；

translations.literal: when enjoying fine food, then think of the two emperors and empress dowager tasting mutton, meat, and curdled milk;
translations.idiomatic: when enjoying fine food, think of the two emperors and empress dowager tasting mutton, meat, and curdled milk;

sentences.zh: 服細暖之衣，則思二帝、母后窮邊絕塞之寒苦；

translations.literal: when wearing fine warm garments, then think of the two emperors and empress dowager suffering extreme cold at remote frontier passes;
translations.idiomatic: when wearing fine warm garments, think of the two emperors and empress dowager suffering extreme cold at remote frontier passes;

sentences.zh: 操與奪之柄，則思二帝、母后語言動作受制於人；

translations.literal: when wielding the power to reward and punish, then think of the two emperors and empress dowager's words and actions constrained by others;
translations.idiomatic: when wielding the power to reward and punish, think of the two emperors and empress dowager's words and actions constrained by others;

sentences.zh: 享嬪御之適，則思二帝、母后誰為之使令；
