translations.literal: when enjoying the company of palace ladies, then think who serves and commands the two emperors and empress dowager;
translations.idiomatic: when enjoying the company of palace ladies, think who serves and commands the two emperors and empress dowager;

sentences.zh: 對臣下之朝，則思二帝、母后誰為之尊禮。

translations.literal: when facing the court of ministers, then think who honors and esteems the two emperors and empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: when facing the court of ministers, think who honors and esteems the two emperors and empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 思之又思，兢兢栗栗，聖心不倦，而天不為之助順者，萬無是理也。」

translations.literal: Reflect again and again, trembling with caution—if the sage heart does not weary yet Heaven does not lend its aid, there is no such principle."
translations.idiomatic: Reflect again and again, trembling with caution—if the sage heart does not weary yet Heaven does not lend its aid, there is no such principle."

sentences.zh: 至是復申前說，曰：「今罪己之詔數下，而天未悔禍，實有所未至耳。」

translations.literal: At this time he reiterated his earlier argument, saying: "Now proclamations of self-blame have been issued repeatedly, yet Heaven has not turned from calamity—there is indeed something still lacking."
translations.idiomatic: At this time he reiterated his earlier argument, saying: "Now proclamations of self-blame have been issued repeatedly, yet Heaven has not turned from calamity—there is indeed something still lacking."

sentences.zh: 且曰：「天時人事至此極矣，陛下睹今日之勢與去年孰愈？

translations.literal: And he said: "Heaven's signs and human affairs have reached the extreme; does Your Majesty see whether today's situation is better or worse than last year?
translations.idiomatic: And he said: "Heaven's signs and human affairs have reached the extreme. Does Your Majesty see whether today's situation is better or worse than last year?

sentences.zh: 而朝廷之措置施設，與前日未始異也。

translations.literal: Yet the court's arrangements and institutions differ in no way from days past.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the court's arrangements and institutions differ in no way from days past.

sentences.zh: 俟其如維揚之變而後言之，則雖斥逐大臣，無救於禍。

translations.literal: To wait until something like the Weiyang disaster occurs before speaking—even if great ministers are dismissed, it will not remedy the harm.
translations.idiomatic: To wait until something like the Weiyang disaster occurs before speaking—even if great ministers are dismissed, it will not remedy the harm.

sentences.zh: 漢制災異策免三公，今任宰相者，雖有勳勞，然其器識不足以斡旋機務。

translations.literal: Under Han institutions, strange disasters led to removing the Three Excellencies; today's chief councilors, though they have merit, lack the capacity and judgment to turn critical affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han institutions, strange disasters led to removing the Three Excellencies. Today's chief councilors, though they have merit, lack the capacity and judgment to turn critical affairs.

sentences.zh: 願更擇文武全材、海內所共推者，親擢而並用之。

translations.literal: I wish you would instead select men of complete civil and military talent whom the realm jointly esteems, elevate them personally, and employ them together.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that men of complete civil and military talent whom the realm jointly esteems be selected, elevated personally, and employed together.

sentences.zh: 上書論事，或有切直，宜加褒擢以來言路。」

translations.literal: Those who submit memorials discussing affairs, even if cutting and blunt, should be praised and promoted to open the path of speech."
translations.idiomatic: Those who submit memorials discussing affairs, even if cutting and blunt, should be praised and promoted to open the path of speech."

sentences.zh: 先是，守嘗論呂頤浩不可獨任，張浚不可西去，與上意異，乞補外。

translations.literal: Earlier Shou had argued that Lü Yihao should not hold sole power and Zhang Jun should not go west—differing from the emperor's view—and requested an outside appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhang Shou had argued that Lü Yihao should not hold sole power and Zhang Jun should not go west—differing from the emperor's view—and requested an outside appointment.

sentences.zh: 除禮部侍郎，不拜，上命呂頤浩至政事堂，諭以正人端士不宜輕去，守始受命。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Minister of Rites but did not accept; the emperor ordered Lü Yihao to the Hall of Administration to instruct him that upright gentlemen should not lightly leave, and Shou then accepted.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Minister of Rites but did not accept. The emperor ordered Lü Yihao to the Hall of Administration to instruct him that upright gentlemen should not lightly leave, and Zhang Shou then accepted.

sentences.zh: 殿中侍御史趙鼎入對，論守無故下遷，上曰：「以其資淺。」

translations.literal: Palace Diarist Zhao Ding entered audience and argued that Shou had been demoted without cause; the emperor said: "Because his qualifications are shallow."
translations.idiomatic: Palace Diarist Zhao Ding entered audience and argued that Zhang Shou had been demoted without cause. The emperor said: "Because his qualifications are shallow."

sentences.zh: 鼎曰：「言事官無他過，願陛下毋沮其氣。」

translations.literal: Ding said: "The remonstrating official is without other fault; I wish Your Majesty not to dampen his spirit."
translations.idiomatic: Ding said: "The remonstrating official is without other fault. I ask Your Majesty not to dampen his spirit."

sentences.zh: 於是遷翰林學士、知制誥。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was promoted to Hanlin Academician and Drafting Director.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was promoted to Hanlin Academician and Drafting Director.

sentences.zh: 九月，拜端明殿學士、同簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he was appointed Academician of the Hall of Manifest Brightness and Concurrent Co-signatory of the Military Affairs Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he was appointed Academician of the Hall of Manifest Brightness and Concurrent Co-signatory of the Military Affairs Commission.

sentences.zh: 扈從由海道至永嘉，回至會稽。

translations.literal: He accompanied the emperor by sea route to Yongjia, then returned to Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor by sea to Yongjia, then returned to Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 四年五月，除參知政事，守嘗薦汪伯彥，沈與求劾其短，以資政殿學士提舉洞霄宮。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year he was appointed Vice Grand Councilor; Shou had once recommended Wang Boyan, and Shen Yuqiu impeached him for faults, so he was made Academician of the Hall of Assisting Governance and Commissioner of the Dongxiao Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fourth year he was appointed Vice Grand Councilor. Zhang Shou had once recommended Wang Boyan, and Shen Yuqiu impeached him for faults, so he was made Academician of the Hall of Assisting Governance and Commissioner of the Dongxiao Palace.

sentences.zh: 未幾，知紹興府。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Prefect of Shaoxing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Prefect of Shaoxing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 尋以內祠兼侍讀，守力辭，改知福州。

translations.literal: Soon he was assigned an inner palace commission concurrently as Imperial Reader; Shou vigorously declined and was instead made Prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was assigned an inner palace commission concurrently as Imperial Reader. Zhang Shou vigorously declined and was instead made Prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 時右司員外郎張宗臣請令福建築城，守奏：「福州城于晉太康三年，偽閩增廣至六千七百餘步，國初削平已久，公私困弊，請俟他年。」

translations.literal: At that time Right Assistant Department Director Zhang Zongchen requested that Fujian build city walls. Shou submitted a memorial: "Fuzhou's walls were built in the third year of the Taikang reign of Jin; the false Min state expanded them to more than six thousand seven hundred paces. Since the dynasty's founding suppressed them long ago, public and private resources are exhausted and distressed—I request postponement to another year."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Right Assistant Department Director Zhang Zongchen requested that Fujian build city walls. Zhang Shou submitted a memorial: "Fuzhou's walls were built in the third year of the Taikang reign of Jin; the false Min state expanded them to more than six thousand seven hundred paces. Since the dynasty's founding suppressed them long ago, public and private resources are exhausted and distressed. I request postponement to another year."

sentences.zh: 遂止。

translations.literal: The proposal was halted.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was halted.

sentences.zh: 尋以變易度牒錢百萬餘緡輸之行在，助國用。

translations.literal: Soon he converted ordination certificates into more than a million strings of cash and sent them to the mobile court to assist state expenditures.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he converted ordination certificates into more than a million strings of cash and sent them to the mobile court to assist state expenditures.

sentences.zh: 時劉豫導金人寇淮，上次平江，諸將獻俘者相踵，守聞之，上疏曰：「今以獻俘誠皆金人，或借諸國，則戮之可也。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Yu guided the Jurchens to raid the Huai region; the emperor stopped at Pingjiang, and generals offering captive presentations followed one after another. Learning of this, Shou submitted a memorial saying: "If those presented as captives are truly Jurchens, or borrowed from other states, then executing them is acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liu Yu guided the Jurchens to raid the Huai region. The emperor stopped at Pingjiang, and generals offering captive presentations followed one after another. Learning of this, Zhang Shou submitted a memorial saying: "If those presented as captives are truly Jurchens, or borrowed from other states, then executing them is acceptable.

sentences.zh: 至如兩河、山東之民，皆陛下赤子，驅迫以來，豈得已哉？

translations.literal: But as for the people of the Two He and Shandong, all are Your Majesty's own children, driven and forced here—how could they have helped it?
translations.idiomatic: But as for the people of the Two He and Shandong, all are Your Majesty's own children, driven and forced here—how could they have helped it?

sentences.zh: 且諭以恩信，貸之使歸，願留者亦聽，則賊兵可不戰而潰。」

translations.literal: If they are instructed with grace and good faith, released to return home, and those wishing to stay are also permitted, then the enemy troops can dissolve without fighting."
translations.idiomatic: If they are instructed with grace and good faith, released to return home, and those wishing to stay are also permitted, then the enemy troops can dissolve without fighting."

sentences.zh: 金人既遁，詔諸將渡江追擊，守復上疏，以敵情難測，願留劉光世控禦諸渡。

translations.literal: After the Jurchens fled, an edict ordered generals to cross the river in pursuit. Shou again submitted a memorial, saying the enemy's intentions were hard to gauge and requesting that Liu Guangshi be kept to guard the crossings.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jurchens fled, an edict ordered generals to cross the river in pursuit. Zhang Shou again submitted a memorial, saying the enemy's intentions were hard to gauge and requesting that Liu Guangshi be kept to guard the crossings.

sentences.zh: 上既還臨安，又詔問守以攻戰之利、守備之宜、綏懷之略、措置之方，守言：

translations.literal: After the emperor returned to Lin'an, he again issued an edict asking Shou about the advantages of attack and defense, proper defensive measures, policies of pacification, and methods of arrangement. Shou said:
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor returned to Lin'an, he again issued an edict asking Zhang Shou about the advantages of attack and defense, proper defensive measures, policies of pacification, and methods of arrangement. Zhang Shou said:

sentences.zh: 明詔四事，臣以為莫急於措置，措置苟當，則余不足為陛下道矣。

translations.literal: Your clear edict on four matters—I think nothing is more urgent than arrangement; if arrangement is properly done, then the rest need not be told to Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: "Your clear edict on four matters—I think nothing is more urgent than arrangement. If arrangement is properly done, the rest need not be told to Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 臣請言措置之大略，其一措置軍旅，其二措置糧食。

translations.literal: Your subject asks to speak of the general outline of arrangement: first, arranging the armies; second, arranging provisions.
translations.idiomatic: "Your subject asks to speak of the general outline of arrangement: first, arranging the armies; second, arranging provisions."

sentences.zh: 神武中軍當專衛行在，而以餘軍分戍三路，一軍駐於淮東，一軍駐於淮西，一軍駐鄂、岳或荊南，擇要害之處以處之。

translations.literal: The Central Army of the Divine Martial Guard should exclusively protect the mobile court, while the remaining armies are divided to garrison three routes—one army stationed in eastern Huai, one in western Huai, one at Ezhou, Yuezhou, or Jingnan, placing them at strategic points.
translations.idiomatic: "The Central Army of the Divine Martial Guard should exclusively protect the mobile court, while the remaining armies are divided to garrison three routes—one army stationed in eastern Huai, one in western Huai, one at Ezhou, Yuezhou, or Jingnan, placing them at strategic points."

sentences.zh: 使北至關輔，西抵川、陝，血脈相通，號令相聞，有唇齒輔車之勢，則自江而南可奠枕而臥也。

translations.literal: Let them reach north to Guanfu and west to Sichuan and Shaanxi, with arteries connected and commands heard mutually, having the mutual-support relation of lips and teeth and the chariot's outer wheel—then south of the Yangzi one may rest with head on pillow.
translations.idiomatic: "Let them reach north to Guanfu and west to Sichuan and Shaanxi, with supply lines connected and orders communicated, so that they possess the mutual reliance of lips and teeth—then south of the Yangzi one may rest secure."

sentences.zh: 然今之大將皆握重兵，貴極富溢，前無祿利之望，退無誅罰之憂，故朝廷之勢日削，兵將之權日重。

translations.literal: Yet today's great generals all hold heavy armies, rank at the extreme and wealth overflowing; advance brings no hope of salary and benefits, retreat brings no fear of punishment and execution—hence the court's power daily declines and the generals' authority daily grows heavy.
translations.idiomatic: "Yet today's great generals all hold heavy armies, rank at the extreme and wealth overflowing. Advance brings no hope of salary and benefits, retreat brings no fear of punishment—hence the court's power daily declines and the generals' authority daily grows."

sentences.zh: 而又為大將者，萬一有稱病而賜罷，或卒然不諱，則所統之眾將安屬耶？

translations.literal: Furthermore, for those who are great generals, if by chance one claims illness and is dismissed by imperial grace, or suddenly dies without forewarning, to whom will the troops under his command belong?
translations.idiomatic: "Furthermore, for those who are great generals, if one claims illness and is dismissed, or suddenly dies without forewarning, to whom will the troops under his command belong?"

sentences.zh: 臣謂宜拔擢麾下之將，使為統制，每將不過五千人，棋布四路，朝廷號令徑達其軍，分合使令悉由朝廷，可以有為也。

translations.literal: Your subject holds that subordinate generals under them should be promoted to serve as commanders, each commanding no more than five thousand men, arrayed like chess pieces on four routes, with court orders reaching their armies directly—deployment and withdrawal, orders and commands all from the court—then something can be accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: "Your subject holds that subordinate generals should be promoted to serve as commanders, each commanding no more than five thousand men, arrayed like chess pieces on four routes, with court orders reaching their armies directly—deployment, withdrawal, and commands all from the court—then something can be accomplished."

sentences.zh: 何謂措置軍食？

translations.literal: What is meant by arranging army provisions?
translations.idiomatic: What is meant by arranging army provisions?

sentences.zh: 諸軍既分屯諸路，則所患者財谷轉輸也。

translations.literal: Since the armies are already divided and encamped on various circuits, what is to be worried about is the transport of funds and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Since the armies are already divided and encamped on various circuits, what is to be worried about is the transport of funds and grain.

sentences.zh: 祖宗以來，每歲上供六百餘萬，出於東南轉輸，未嘗以為病也。

translations.literal: Since the founders, each year more than six million in tribute supply came from transport through the southeast, and this was never regarded as a burden.
translations.idiomatic: Since the founders, each year more than six million in tribute supply came from transport through the southeast, and this was never regarded as a burden.

sentences.zh: 今宜舉兩浙之粟以餉淮東，江西之粟以餉淮西，荊湖之粟以餉鄂、岳、荊南。

translations.literal: Now one should use the grain of the Two Zhes to supply eastern Huai, the grain of Jiangxi to supply western Huai, and the grain of Jinghu to supply Ezhou, Yuezhou, and Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Now one should use the grain of the Two Zhes to supply eastern Huai, the grain of Jiangxi to supply western Huai, and the grain of Jinghu to supply Ezhou, Yuezhou, and Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 量所用之數，責漕臣將輸，而歸其餘於行在，錢帛亦然，恐未至於不足也。

translations.literal: Estimate the amount needed, charge transport officials to deliver supplies, and return the remainder to the mobile court—the same for cash and cloth—probably not to the point of insufficiency.
translations.idiomatic: Estimate the amount needed, charge transport officials to deliver supplies, and return the remainder to the mobile court—the same for cash and cloth—and it probably would not prove insufficient.

sentences.zh: 錢糧無乏絕之患，然後戒飭諸將，不得侵擾州縣，以復業之民戶口多寡，為諸將殿最，歲核實而黜陟之。

translations.literal: With no danger of shortage in funds and grain, then admonish the generals not to harass prefectures and counties; use the number of households among the people restored to their livelihoods as the ranking of generals' merit and demerit, verify annually and promote or dismiss accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: With no danger of shortage in funds and grain, admonish the generals not to harass prefectures and counties. Use the number of households among the people restored to their livelihoods as the measure of each general's merit, verify annually, and promote or dismiss accordingly.

sentences.zh: 如是措置既定，俟至防秋，復遣大臣為之統督，使諸路之兵首尾相應，綏懷之略亦在是矣。

translations.literal: If arrangement is thus established, wait until the autumn defense season, then again send great ministers to oversee and command, causing armies of the various circuits to respond from head to tail—the policy of pacification is also in this.
translations.idiomatic: If arrangement is thus established, wait until the autumn defense season, then send great ministers to oversee and command so that armies of the various circuits respond in concert—the policy of pacification lies in this as well.

sentences.zh: 究其本原，則在陛下內修德而外修政耳。

translations.literal: Probing to its root cause, it lies in Your Majesty cultivating virtue within and cultivating governance without.
translations.idiomatic: Probing to its root cause, it lies in Your Majesty cultivating virtue within and cultivating governance without.

sentences.zh: 閩自范汝為之擾，公私赤立，守在鎮四年，撫綏凋瘵，且請於朝，蠲除福州所貸常平緡錢十五萬。

translations.literal: Since Fan Ruwei's disturbances in Min, public and private were stripped bare; Shou was at the post four years, comforting and pacifying the devastated and afflicted, and also requested of the court remission of one hundred fifty thousand strings of Ever-Normal granary money loaned to Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Since Fan Ruwei's disturbances in Min, public and private resources were stripped bare. Zhang Shou served there four years, comforting the devastated populace, and also requested of the court remission of one hundred fifty thousand strings of Ever-Normal granary money loaned to Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 累請去郡，以提舉萬壽觀兼侍讀召還，甫兩月，復引病丐去，知平江府，力丐祠以歸。

translations.literal: He repeatedly requested to leave the prefecture; summoned back as Commissioner of the Wanshou Abbey concurrently Imperial Reader—barely two months, again citing illness and begging to leave; appointed Prefect of Pingjiang Prefecture; vigorously begged a temple commission to return home.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly requested to leave the prefecture and was summoned back as Commissioner of the Wanshou Abbey concurrently Imperial Reader. Barely two months later, he again cited illness and begged to leave, was appointed Prefect of Pingjiang Prefecture, and vigorously begged a temple commission to return home.

sentences.zh: 六年十二月，召見，即日除參知政事，明日兼權樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the sixth year he was summoned for audience; that same day he was appointed Vice Grand Councilor; the next day he concurrently served as Acting Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the sixth year he was summoned for audience. That same day he was appointed Vice Grand Councilor; the next day he concurrently served as Acting Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 七年，張浚罷劉光世兵柄，而欲以呂祉往淮西撫諭諸軍，守以為不可，浚不從，守曰：「必曰改圖，亦須得聞望素高、能服諸將之心者乃可。」

translations.literal: In the seventh year Zhang Jun removed Liu Guangshi's military authority and wished to send Lü Zhi to western Huai to reassure the armies. Shou thought it inadvisable; Jun did not listen. Shou said: "If one must change plans, one still needs someone whose reputation is already high and who can win the generals' hearts."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Zhang Jun removed Liu Guangshi's military authority and wished to send Lü Zhi to western Huai to reassure the armies. Zhang Shou thought it inadvisable; Zhang Jun did not listen. Zhang Shou said: "If one must change plans, one still needs someone whose reputation is already high and who can win the generals' hearts."

sentences.zh: 浚不聽，遂有酈瓊之變。

translations.literal: Jun did not listen, and thereafter came Li Qiong's mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun did not listen, and thereafter came Li Qiong's mutiny.

sentences.zh: 及臺諫父章論浚，御批安置嶺表，赴鼎不即行，守力解上曰：「浚為陛下捍兩淮，罷劉光世，正以其眾烏合不為用，今其驗矣，群臣從而媒蘖其短，臣恐後之繼者，必以浚為鑒，誰肯為陛下任事乎？」

translations.literal: When censorial officials submitted repeated memorials criticizing Jun, the emperor annotated to banish him to Lingnan; Zhao Ding did not immediately act; Shou forcefully pleaded with the emperor, saying: "Jun defended the Two Huai for Your Majesty and removed Liu Guangshi precisely because his troops were a motley rabble of no use—now that has been proven. If the ministers follow by magnifying his faults, I fear those who come after will take Jun as a warning—who then will be willing to take on affairs for Your Majesty?"
translations.idiomatic: When censorial officials submitted repeated memorials criticizing Zhang Jun, the emperor annotated to banish him to Lingnan. Zhao Ding did not immediately act. Zhang Shou forcefully pleaded with the emperor, saying: "Zhang Jun defended the Two Huai for Your Majesty and removed Liu Guangshi precisely because his troops were a motley rabble of no use—now that has been proven. If the ministers follow by magnifying his faults, I fear those who come after will take Zhang Jun as a warning—who then will be willing to take on affairs for Your Majesty?"

sentences.zh: 浚謫永州，守亦引咎請去，弗許。

translations.literal: Jun was demoted to Yongzhou; Shou also took blame and requested to leave, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun was demoted to Yongzhou. Zhang Shou also took blame and requested to leave, but was not permitted.

sentences.zh: 八年正月，上自建康將還臨安，守言：「建康自六朝為帝王都，江流險闊，氣象雄偉，且據都會以經理中原，依險阻以捍禦強敵，可為別都以圖恢復。」

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighth year, as the emperor was about to return from Jiankang to Lin'an, Shou said: "Jiankang has been an imperial capital since the Six Dynasties; the river flows perilously wide, its aspect grand and imposing. Moreover, holding this metropolis one may manage the Central Plains and rely on natural barriers to repel strong enemies—it can serve as a secondary capital to plan recovery."
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eighth year, as the emperor was about to return from Jiankang to Lin'an, Zhang Shou said: "Jiankang has been an imperial capital since the Six Dynasties; the river flows perilously wide, its aspect grand and imposing. Moreover, holding this metropolis one may manage the Central Plains and rely on natural barriers to repel strong enemies—it can serve as a secondary capital to plan recovery."

sentences.zh: 鼎持不可，守力求去，以資政殿大學士知婺州，尋改洪州，兼江南西路安撫使。

translations.literal: Ding held it inadvisable; Shou vigorously sought to leave and was made Academician of the Hall of Assisting Governance as Prefect of Wuzhou, soon changed to Hongzhou, concurrently Pacification Commissioner of Jiangnan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ding held it inadvisable. Zhang Shou vigorously sought to leave and was made Academician of the Hall of Assisting Governance as Prefect of Wuzhou, soon changed to Hongzhou, concurrently Pacification Commissioner of Jiangnan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 入對，時江西盜賊未息，上問以弭盜之策，守曰：「莫先德政，伺其不悛，然後加之以兵。」

translations.literal: Entering audience, bandits in Jiangxi had not yet been pacified; the emperor asked about policies to suppress banditry. Shou said: "Nothing comes before virtuous governance; wait until they fail to reform, then add military force."
translations.idiomatic: Entering audience, bandits in Jiangxi had not yet been pacified. The emperor asked about policies to suppress banditry. Zhang Shou said: "Nothing comes before virtuous governance. Wait until they fail to reform, then add military force."

sentences.zh: 因請出師屯要害。

translations.literal: He then requested to dispatch troops to encamp at strategic points.
translations.idiomatic: He then requested to dispatch troops to encamp at strategic points.

sentences.zh: 既至部，揭榜郡邑，開諭禍福，約以期限，許之自新，不數月盜平。

translations.literal: Once he reached his jurisdiction, he posted proclamations in prefectures and counties, openly instructing on fortune and disaster, setting deadlines and permitting self-renewal—in less than several months banditry was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Once he reached his jurisdiction, he posted proclamations in prefectures and counties, openly instructing on fortune and disaster, setting deadlines and permitting self-renewal. In less than several months banditry was pacified.

sentences.zh: 後徙知紹興府。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to serve as Prefect of Shaoxing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was transferred to serve as Prefect of Shaoxing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 會朝廷遣三使者括諸路財賦，所至以鞭撻立威，韓球在會稽，所斂五十餘萬緡。

translations.literal: It happened that the court dispatched three envoys to requisition the wealth and taxes of the various circuits; wherever they went they established authority through flogging. Han Qiu was in Kuaiji and collected more than five hundred thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that the court dispatched three envoys to requisition the wealth and taxes of the various circuits; wherever they went they established authority through flogging. Han Qiu was in Kuaiji and collected more than five hundred thousand strings.

sentences.zh: 守既視事，即求入覲，為上言之，詔追還三使。

translations.literal: Once Shou assumed office, he immediately requested an audience to report this to the emperor; an edict recalled the three envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhang Shou assumed office, he immediately requested an audience to report this to the emperor. An edict recalled the three envoys.

sentences.zh: 時秦檜當國，不悅，守亦不自安，復奉祠。

translations.literal: At that time Qin Hui held power and was displeased; Shou also felt ill at ease and again accepted a temple commission.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Qin Hui held power and was displeased. Zhang Shou also felt ill at ease and again accepted a temple commission.

sentences.zh: 建康謀帥，上曰：「建康重地，用大臣有德望者，惟張守可。」

translations.literal: When Jiankang sought a commander, the emperor said: "Jiankang is a vital post; of great ministers with virtue and reputation, only Zhang Shou will do."
translations.idiomatic: When Jiankang sought a commander, the emperor said: "Jiankang is a vital post. Of great ministers with virtue and reputation, only Zhang Shou will do."

sentences.zh: 至鎮數月薨。

translations.literal: Several months after reaching the post he died.
translations.idiomatic: Several months after reaching the post he died.

sentences.zh: 守嘗薦秦檜于時宰張浚，及檜為樞密使，同朝。

translations.literal: Shou had once recommended Qin Hui to the chief councilor Zhang Jun; when Hui became Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs, they served in the same court.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shou had once recommended Qin Hui to the chief councilor Zhang Jun. When Hui became Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs, they served in the same court.

sentences.zh: 一日，守在省閣執浚手曰：「守前者誤公矣。

translations.literal: One day Shou took Jun's hand in the provincial pavilion and said: "Shou wronged you before.
translations.idiomatic: One day Zhang Shou took Zhang Jun's hand in the provincial pavilion and said: "I wronged you before.

sentences.zh: 今同班列，與之朝夕相處，觀其趨向，有患失之心，公宜力陳於上。」

translations.literal: Now serving in the same ranks and associating with him morning and evening, observing his inclinations, he has a mind fearful of gain and loss—you should forcefully report this to the emperor."
translations.idiomatic: Now serving in the same ranks and associating with him morning and evening, observing his inclinations, he has a mind fearful of gain and loss. You should forcefully report this to the emperor."

sentences.zh: 守在江右，以郡縣供億科擾，上疏請蠲和買，罷和糴。

translations.literal: When Shou was in Jiangyou, because prefectures and counties were harassed by supply requisitions, he submitted a memorial requesting remission of harmonized purchases and abolition of harmonized grain levies.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Shou was in Jiangyou, because prefectures and counties were harassed by supply requisitions, he submitted a memorial requesting remission of harmonized purchases and abolition of harmonized grain levies.

sentences.zh: 上欲行之，時秦檜方損度支為月進，且日憂四方財用之不至，見守疏，怒曰：「張帥何損國如是？」

translations.literal: The emperor wished to implement it, but at that time Qin Hui was just cutting the Revenue Bureau's funds for monthly tribute and daily worried that revenue from the four quarters would not arrive. Seeing Shou's memorial, he angrily said: "Why does Marshal Zhang harm the state like this?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to implement it, but at that time Qin Hui was just cutting the Revenue Bureau's funds for monthly tribute and daily worried that revenue from the four quarters would not arrive. Seeing Zhang Shou's memorial, he angrily said: "Why does Marshal Zhang harm the state like this?"

sentences.zh: 守聞之，歎曰：「彼謂損國，乃益國也。」

translations.literal: Learning of this, Shou sighed and said: "What he calls harming the state is actually benefiting the state."
translations.idiomatic: Learning of this, Zhang Shou sighed and said: "What he calls harming the state is actually benefiting the state."

sentences.zh: 卒諡文靖。

translations.literal: Upon death he was posthumously titled Wenjing.
translations.idiomatic: Upon death he was posthumously titled Wenjing.

sentences.zh: 孫抑，戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: His grandson Sun Yi was Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Sun Yi was Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 富直柔

translations.literal: Fu Zhirou
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhirou

sentences.zh: 富直柔，字季申，宰相弼之孫也。

translations.literal: Fu Zhirou, style name Jishen, was a grandson of Grand Councilor Bi.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhirou, style name Jishen, was a grandson of Grand Councilor Fu Bi.

sentences.zh: 以父任補官。

translations.literal: He received office through his father's yin privilege.
translations.idiomatic: He received office through his father's yin privilege.

sentences.zh: 少敏悟，有才名。

translations.literal: In youth he was quick and perceptive, with a reputation for talent.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was quick and perceptive, with a reputation for talent.

sentences.zh: 靖康初，晁說之奇其文，薦於朝，召賜同進士出身，除秘書省正字。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingkang era, Chao Yuezhi marveled at his writing and recommended him to the court; summoned and granted jinshi status by special decree, he was appointed Corrector in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jingkang era, Chao Yuezhi marveled at his writing and recommended him to the court. Summoned and granted jinshi status by special decree, he was appointed Corrector in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 建炎二年，召近臣舉所知，禮部侍郎張浚以直柔應。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Jianyan era, close ministers were summoned to recommend men they knew; Vice Minister of Rites Zhang Jun nominated Zhirou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Jianyan era, close ministers were summoned to recommend men they knew. Vice Minister of Rites Zhang Jun nominated Zhirou.

sentences.zh: 詔授著作佐郎，尋除禮部員外郎、起居舍人，遷右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him Assistant Compiler; soon he was made Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites and Diarist of Attendance, then promoted to Right Remonstrating Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed him Assistant Compiler. Soon he was made Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites and Diarist of Attendance, then promoted to Right Remonstrating Grandee.

sentences.zh: 範致虛自謫籍中召入，直柔力言致虛不當復用，出知鼎州。

translations.literal: Fan Zhixu was recalled from the rolls of the banished; Zhirou forcefully argued that Zhixu should not be reused and was sent out as Prefect of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhixu was recalled from the rolls of the banished. Zhirou forcefully argued that Zhixu should not be reused and was sent out as Prefect of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 遷給事中。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 醫官、團練使王繼先以覃恩轉防禦使，法當回授，得旨特與換武功大夫。

translations.literal: The medical officer and regimental training commissioner Wang Jixian, through a grace amnesty, was transferred to Defender-in-Chief; by law he should have returned the appointment, but received an imperial order specially exchanging it for Grandee of Military Merit.
translations.idiomatic: The medical officer and regimental training commissioner Wang Jixian, through a grace amnesty, was transferred to Defender-in-Chief. By law he should have returned the appointment, but received an imperial order specially exchanging it for Grandee of Military Merit.

sentences.zh: 直柔論：「繼先以計換授，既授之後，轉行官資，除授差遣，更無所礙。

translations.literal: Zhirou argued: "Jixian used a stratagem to exchange appointments; once the appointment is granted, advancing in official rank and receiving appointments and commissions will meet no further obstacle.
translations.idiomatic: Zhirou argued: "Jixian used a stratagem to exchange appointments. Once the appointment is granted, advancing in official rank and receiving appointments and commissions will meet no further obstacle.

sentences.zh: 且武功大夫惟有戰功、曆邊任、負材武者乃遷，不可以輕授。」

translations.literal: Moreover, Grandee of Military Merit is conferred only on those with battle merit, experience in frontier service, and proven martial talent—it must not be lightly granted."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Grandee of Military Merit is conferred only on those with battle merit, experience in frontier service, and proven martial talent—it must not be lightly granted."

sentences.zh: 上謂宰相范宗尹曰：「此除出自朕意。

translations.literal: The emperor told Grand Councilor Fan Zongyin: "This appointment came from my own intent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Grand Councilor Fan Zongyin: "This appointment came from my own intent.

sentences.zh: 今直柔抗論，朕屈意從之，以伸直言之氣。」

translations.literal: Now Zhirou remonstrated against it; I yielded my intent to follow him, to give straight speech its full force."
translations.idiomatic: Now Zhirou remonstrated against it. I yielded my intent to follow him, to give straight speech its full force."

sentences.zh: 四年，遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was promoted to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was promoted to Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 直柔請罷右司侯延慶，而以蘇遲代之，上曰：「臺諫以拾遺補過為職，不當薦某人為某官。」

translations.literal: Zhirou requested dismissal of Right Assistant Department Director Hou Yanqing and replacement by Su Chi. The emperor said: "Censorial remonstrators have the duty of picking up omissions and remedying faults—they should not recommend a certain person for a certain office."
translations.idiomatic: Zhirou requested dismissal of Right Assistant Department Director Hou Yanqing and replacement by Su Chi. The emperor said: "Censorial remonstrators have the duty of picking up omissions and remedying faults—they should not recommend a certain person for a certain office."

sentences.zh: 於是延慶改禮部員外郎，而遲為太常少卿。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yanqing was changed to Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites and Chi to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Yanqing was changed to Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites and Chi to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 十月，除端明殿學士、簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he was appointed Academician of the Hall of Enduring Brightness and Co-signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was appointed Academician of the Hall of Enduring Brightness and Co-signatory of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 故事，簽書有以員外郎為之，而無三丞為之者。

translations.literal: By precedent, co-signatories had been Vice Directors, but none had been one of the three assistant commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, co-signatories had been Vice Directors, but none had been one of the three assistant commissioners.

sentences.zh: 中書言非舊典，時直柔為奉議郎，乃特遷朝奉郎。

translations.literal: The Secretariat said this was not old precedent; at the time Zhirou was Gentleman for Promoting Righteousness, so he was specially promoted to Gentleman for Court Audience.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat said this was not old precedent. At the time Zhirou was Gentleman for Promoting Righteousness, so he was specially promoted to Gentleman for Court Audience.

sentences.zh: 自是寄祿官三丞除二府者，遷員外郎，自直柔始，遂為例。

translations.literal: From then on, when salary-only officials among the three assistant commissioners were appointed to the two bureaus, they were promoted to Vice Director—beginning with Zhirou, this became precedent.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, when salary-only officials among the three assistant commissioners were appointed to the two bureaus, they were promoted to Vice Director—beginning with Zhirou, this became precedent.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年，詔禮部太常寺討論隆祐太后冊禮，范宗尹曰：「太母前後廢斥，實出章惇、蔡京，人皆知非二聖之過。」

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxing, an edict ordered the Ministry of Rites and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to deliberate on the patent ceremony for Empress Dowager Longyou. Fan Zongyin said: "The Grand Empress Dowager was deposed and displaced before and after, and this truly came from Zhang Dun and Cai Jing. All know it was not the fault of the Two Sovereigns."
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shaoxing, an edict ordered the Ministry of Rites and the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to deliberate on the patent ceremony for Empress Dowager Longyou. Fan Zongyin said: "The Grand Empress Dowager was deposed and displaced before and after, and this truly came from Zhang Dun and Cai Jing. All know it was not the fault of the Two Sovereigns."

sentences.zh: 直柔曰：「陛下推崇隆祐，天下以為當，然人亦不以為非哲廟與上皇意，願陛下勿復致疑。」

translations.literal: Zhirou said: "Your Majesty honors Longyou, and the realm holds this proper. Yet people also do not think it contrary to Emperor Zhezong's and the retired emperor's intent. I beg Your Majesty not to raise doubts again."
translations.idiomatic: Zhirou said: "Your Majesty honors Longyou, and the realm holds this proper. Yet people also do not think it contrary to Emperor Zhezong's and the retired emperor's intent. I beg Your Majesty not to raise doubts again."

sentences.zh: 乃命禮官討論典禮。

translations.literal: Thereupon ritual officers were ordered to deliberate on the ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon ritual officers were ordered to deliberate on the ceremony.

sentences.zh: 既而王居正言：「太后隆名定位，已正于元符，宜用欽聖詔，奏告天地宗廟，其典禮不須討論。」

translations.literal: Soon Wang Juzheng said: "The empress dowager's exalted name and rank were already established in the Yuanfu era. The Qinsheng edict should be used to report to Heaven and Earth and the ancestral temples. This ceremony need not be deliberated."
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wang Juzheng said: "The empress dowager's exalted name and rank were already established in the Yuanfu era. The Qinsheng edict should be used to report to Heaven and Earth and the ancestral temples. This ceremony need not be deliberated."

sentences.zh: 議遂定。

translations.literal: The deliberation was thereupon settled.
translations.idiomatic: The deliberation was thereupon settled.

sentences.zh: 上虞縣丞婁寅亮上書言宗社大計，欲選太祖諸孫「伯」字行下有賢德者視秩親王，使牧九州，以待皇嗣之生，退處藩服。

translations.literal: Shangyu County Assistant Lou Yinliang submitted a memorial on the great plan for the altars of state and grain, wishing to select from among Emperor Taizu's grandsons of the "Bo" generation one of virtue and treat him with princely rank, entrusting him to govern the nine provinces while awaiting the birth of an imperial heir, then withdrawing to a feudal position.
translations.idiomatic: Shangyu County Assistant Lou Yinliang submitted a memorial on the great plan for the altars of state and grain, wishing to select from among Emperor Taizu's grandsons of the "Bo" generation one of virtue and treat him with princely rank, entrusting him to govern the nine provinces while awaiting the birth of an imperial heir, then withdrawing to a feudal position.

sentences.zh: 疏入，上大歎悟，直柔從而薦之，召赴行在，除監察御史。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the emperor greatly sighed in enlightenment; Zhirou followed by recommending him; summoned to the mobile court, he was appointed Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial entered, the emperor greatly sighed in enlightenment. Zhirou followed by recommending him. Summoned to the mobile court, he was appointed Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 於是孝宗立為普安郡王，以寅亮之言也。

translations.literal: Thereupon Emperor Xiaozong was established as Prince of Pu'an—because of Yinliang's words.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Emperor Xiaozong was established as Prince of Pu'an—because of Yinliang's words.

sentences.zh: 除同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Co-administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Co-administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 侍御史沈與求論直柔附會辛道宗、永宗兄弟得進，並論其所薦右司諫韓璜。

translations.literal: Attending Censor Shen Yuqiu argued that Zhirou had curried favor with the brothers Xin Daozong and Yongzong to advance, and also criticized Han Huang, Right Remonstrator of the Assistant Department, whom he had recommended.
translations.idiomatic: Attending Censor Shen Yuqiu argued that Zhirou had curried favor with the brothers Xin Daozong and Yongzong to advance, and also criticized Han Huang, Right Remonstrator of the Assistant Department, whom he had recommended.

sentences.zh: 先是，直柔嘗短呂頤浩於上前，頤浩與秦檜皆忌之，由是二人俱罷，礌責監潯州酒稅，而直柔以本官提舉洞霄宮。

translations.literal: Earlier Zhirou had spoken ill of Lü Yihao before the emperor; Yihao and Qin Hui both resented him. Thereby both men were dismissed—Huang was punished as Supervisor of the Xunzhou Wine Tax, and Zhirou retained his original rank as Commissioner of the Dongxiao Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhirou had spoken ill of Lü Yihao before the emperor. Yihao and Qin Hui both resented him. Thereby both men were dismissed—Huang was punished as Supervisor of the Xunzhou Wine Tax, and Zhirou retained his original rank as Commissioner of the Dongxiao Palace.

sentences.zh: 六年，丁所生母憂。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he mourned his biological mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he mourned his biological mother.

sentences.zh: 起復資政殿學士、知鎮江府，辭不赴。

translations.literal: Recalled from mourning as Academician of the Hall of Assisting Governance and Prefect of Zhenjiang Prefecture, he declined and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled from mourning as Academician of the Hall of Assisting Governance and Prefect of Zhenjiang Prefecture, he declined and did not go.

sentences.zh: 起知衢州。

translations.literal: Recalled to serve as Prefect of Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to serve as Prefect of Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 以失入死罪，落職奉祠。

translations.literal: For imposing a capital sentence in error, he was demoted and given a temple commission.
translations.idiomatic: For imposing a capital sentence in error, he was demoted and given a temple commission.

sentences.zh: 尋復端明殿學士。

translations.literal: Soon he was restored as Academician of the Hall of Enduring Brightness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was restored as Academician of the Hall of Enduring Brightness.

sentences.zh: 徜徉山澤，放意吟詠，與蘇遲、葉夢得諸人游，以壽終於家。

translations.literal: He wandered among mountains and marshes, giving free rein to poetry and song, associating with Su Chi, Ye Mengde, and others, and died at home of old age.
translations.idiomatic: He wandered among mountains and marshes, giving free rein to poetry and song, associating with Su Chi, Ye Mengde, and others, and died at home of old age.

sentences.zh: 馮康國

translations.literal: Feng Kangguo
translations.idiomatic: Feng Kangguo

sentences.zh: 馮康國，字元通，本名轓，遂寧府人。

translations.literal: Feng Kangguo, style name Yuantong, original name Fan, was a native of Suining Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Kangguo, style name Yuantong, original name Fan, was a native of Suining Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 為太學生，負氣節。

translations.literal: He was a student of the Imperial Academy, possessed of spirited integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He was a student of the Imperial Academy, possessed of spirited integrity.

sentences.zh: 建炎中，高宗次杭州，禮部侍郎張浚以御營參贊軍事留平江。

translations.literal: During the Jianyan era, Emperor Gaozong stopped at Hangzhou; Vice Minister of Rites Zhang Jun, as Military Adviser to the Imperial Camp, remained at Pingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianyan era, Emperor Gaozong stopped at Hangzhou. Vice Minister of Rites Zhang Jun, as Military Adviser to the Imperial Camp, remained at Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 苗、劉作亂，浚外倡帥諸將合兵致討，念傅等居中，欲得辯士往說之。

translations.literal: When Miao and Liu rebelled, Jun outwardly led the generals to combine forces for punitive action; considering that Fu and others held the center, he wished to obtain an eloquent envoy to go persuade them.
translations.idiomatic: When Miao and Liu rebelled, Zhang Jun outwardly led the generals to combine forces for punitive action. Considering that Fu and others held the center, he wished to obtain an eloquent envoy to go persuade them.

sentences.zh: 時轓客浚所，慷慨請行，浚遣之至杭，說傅、正彥曰：「自古宦官亂政，根株相連，若誅鋤必受禍。

translations.literal: At that time Fan was a guest at Jun's residence and boldly volunteered to go; Jun sent him to Hangzhou and he addressed Fu and Zhengyan, saying: "Since antiquity eunuchs who disturbed government had roots and branches linked together—if one uproots and cuts them down, one must suffer harm.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Fan was a guest at Zhang Jun's residence and boldly volunteered to go. Zhang Jun sent him to Hangzhou and he addressed Fu and Zhengyan, saying: "Since antiquity eunuchs who disturbed government had roots and branches linked together—if one uproots and cuts them down, one must suffer harm.

sentences.zh: 今二公一旦為國家去數十年之患，天下蒙福甚大。

translations.literal: Now you two lords at once removed for the state a decades-old scourge—the realm has received great blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Now you two lords at once removed for the state a decades-old scourge—the realm has received great blessing.

sentences.zh: 然主上春秋鼎盛，天下不聞其過，豈可遽傳位於繈褓之子？

translations.literal: Yet the sovereign is in the prime of life; the realm has heard no fault of his—how can the throne be hastily transferred to a child in swaddling clothes?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the sovereign is in the prime of life; the realm has heard no fault of his—how can the throne be hastily transferred to a child in swaddling clothes?

sentences.zh: 且前日名為傳位，其實廢立，二公本心為國，奈何以此負謗天下？」

translations.literal: Moreover, the other day what was called transferring the throne was in fact deposition and installation—you two lords at heart acted for the state; why bear slander from the realm for this?"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the other day what was called transferring the throne was in fact deposition and installation—you two lords at heart acted for the state. Why bear slander from the realm for this?"

sentences.zh: 傅按劍大怒，轓辭氣不屈。

translations.literal: Fu grasped his sword in great anger; Fan's words and bearing did not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Fu grasped his sword in great anger; Fan's words and bearing did not yield.

sentences.zh: 正彥乃善諭之曰：「張侍郎欲復辟固善，然須用面議。」

translations.literal: Zhengyan then kindly instructed him, saying: "Vice Minister Zhang wishes to restore the emperor—that is indeed good, but it must be discussed face to face."
translations.idiomatic: Zhengyan then kindly instructed him, saying: "Vice Minister Zhang wishes to restore the emperor—that is indeed good, but it must be discussed face to face."

sentences.zh: 乃遣轓還，約浚至杭。

translations.literal: He then sent Fan back and arranged for Jun to come to Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Fan back and arranged for Zhang Jun to come to Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 浚復遣轓移書傅等，告以禍福使改。

translations.literal: Jun again sent Fan with a letter to Fu and others, informing them of fortune and disaster to make them change course.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun again sent Fan with a letter to Fu and others, informing them of fortune and disaster to make them change course.

sentences.zh: 既又復傅書，誦言其罪。

translations.literal: Then he again replied to Fu's letter, reciting his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Then he again replied to Fu's letter, reciting his crimes.

sentences.zh: 轓至，傅党馬柔吉訹之曰：「昨張侍郎書不委曲，二公大怒，已發兵出杭矣，君尚敢來耶？」

translations.literal: When Fan arrived, Fu's partisan Ma Rouji intimidated him, saying: "Yesterday Vice Minister Zhang's letter was not tactful; the two lords were greatly angered and have already dispatched troops out of Hangzhou—do you still dare come?"
translations.idiomatic: When Fan arrived, Fu's partisan Ma Rouji intimidated him, saying: "Yesterday Vice Minister Zhang's letter was not tactful. The two lords were greatly angered and have already dispatched troops out of Hangzhou—do you still dare come?"

sentences.zh: 轓曰：「畏則不來，來則不畏。」

translations.literal: Fan said: "If I feared, I would not have come; having come, I do not fear."
translations.idiomatic: Fan said: "If I feared, I would not have come. Having come, I do not fear."

sentences.zh: 王世修欲拘留轓，會浚謬為書遺轓云：「適有客自杭來，方知二公于社稷初無不利之心，甚悔前書之輕易也。」

translations.literal: Wang Shixiu wished to detain Fan, but it happened that Jun falsely wrote a letter to Fan saying: "A guest has just come from Hang—now I know that you two gentlemen from the start had no heart to harm the altars of state; I deeply regret the rashness of my earlier letter."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shixiu wanted to detain Fan, but Zhang Jun forged a letter to him: "A visitor just arrived from Hangzhou—I now see you two never meant harm to the realm, and deeply regret my rash earlier message."

sentences.zh: 傅等見之喜，轓得免。

translations.literal: Fu and the others saw it and rejoiced; Fan was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Fu and his party were delighted, and Fan escaped detention.

sentences.zh: 俄勤王之兵大集，傅等始懼，轓知其可動，乃說宰相朱勝非，以今日之事，當以淵聖皇帝為主，睿聖皇帝宜復為大元帥，少主為皇太侄，太后垂簾。

translations.literal: Soon the armies that came to rescue the throne gathered in great numbers; Fu and the others began to fear; Fan knew they could be moved and thereupon persuaded the chief minister Zhu Shengfei that in today's affair the Deep Sage Emperor should be made sovereign, the Sagely Emperor should again become Grand Marshal, the young lord should be Imperial Nephew Heir, and the empress dowager should rule from behind the curtain.
translations.idiomatic: Soon relief armies massed, and Fu's party grew afraid. Fan saw they could be swayed and persuaded Chief Councilor Zhu Shengfei that Qinzong should be recognized as emperor, Gaozong restored as Grand Marshal, the young emperor made Imperial Nephew Heir, and the empress dowager should rule from behind the curtain.

sentences.zh: 勝非令與傅、正彥議，皆許諾。

translations.literal: Shengfei ordered them to discuss with Fu and Zhengyan; all promised assent.
translations.idiomatic: Shengfei had them negotiate with Fu and Zhengyan, and all agreed.

sentences.zh: 轓又請褒傅、正彥如趙普故事，遂皆賜鐵券。

translations.literal: Fan also requested to honor Fu and Zhengyan after the precedent of Zhao Pu, and thereupon both were granted iron certificates of immunity.
translations.idiomatic: Fan also asked that Fu and Zhengyan be rewarded like Zhao Pu, and both received iron certificates of immunity.

sentences.zh: 詔補轓奉議郎、守兵部員外郎，賜五品服，更名康國。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Fan supplementary Proposal Presenter, acting Vice Director of the Ministry of War, granted fifth-rank robes, and changed his name to Kangguo.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Fan a Proposal Presenter and acting Vice Director of War, granted fifth-rank court dress, and renamed him Kangguo.

sentences.zh: 高宗反正，以張浚宣撫川、陝，浚辟康國主管機宜文字。

translations.literal: When Gaozong restored proper rule, Zhang Jun was made pacification commissioner for Sichuan and Shaanxi; Jun recruited Kangguo as drafter in charge of military planning documents.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozong restored the throne, Zhang Jun was sent to pacify Sichuan and Shaanxi and recruited Kangguo as his planning secretary.

sentences.zh: 浚至蜀，遣康國入奏事，詔進兩官，為荊湖宣諭使。

translations.literal: When Jun reached Shu he sent Kangguo in to report on affairs; an edict advanced him two ranks and made him pacification envoy for Jing and Hu.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun reached Sichuan he sent Kangguo to court; the emperor promoted him two ranks and appointed him envoy to Jing and Hu.

sentences.zh: 康國之行也，上幸浙東，不暇降詔旨，康國以自意為之，言者劾以擅造制書，坐貶秩二等。

translations.literal: On Kangguo's mission the emperor was touring eastern Zhe and had no leisure to issue edicts; Kangguo acted on his own judgment; remonstrators impeached him for usurping the drafting of imperial documents, and he was demoted two ranks in punishment.
translations.idiomatic: On this mission the emperor was touring eastern Zhejiang and could not issue orders in time; Kangguo drafted documents on his own initiative. Critics impeached him for forging imperial documents, and he was demoted two ranks.

sentences.zh: 紹興三年，浚召還，與康國俱赴行在。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shaoxing, Jun was recalled and went with Kangguo together to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: In 1133 Zhang Jun was recalled, and he and Kangguo went together to the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 浚既黜，御史常同因論康國，罷之。

translations.literal: After Jun was dismissed, the censor Chang Tong criticized Kangguo on that account and had him removed.
translations.idiomatic: After Jun was dismissed, Censor Chang Tong attacked Kangguo by association and had him removed from office.

sentences.zh: 起知萬州、湖北轉運判官。

translations.literal: He was raised to administer Wanzhou and serve as transport vice commissioner for Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to govern Wanzhou and serve as transport vice commissioner for Hubei.

sentences.zh: 浚相，入為都官員外郎。

translations.literal: When Jun became chief councilor, Kangguo entered the capital as Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jun became chief councilor, Kangguo entered the capital as Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 康國言：「四川稅色，祖宗以來，正稅重者科折輕，正稅輕者科折重，科折權衡與稅平准，故無偏重。

translations.literal: Kangguo said: "In Sichuan's tax categories, since the ancestral founders, where the regular tax was heavy the commutation levy was light, and where the regular tax was light the commutation levy was heavy—the balance of commutation and the leveling of tax were matched, and therefore there was no overweighting.
translations.idiomatic: Kangguo said: "In Sichuan's tax system, since the founding emperors heavy regular taxes were matched with light commutation levies and light regular taxes with heavy commutation, keeping the scales even—so no category was overburdened.

sentences.zh: 近年監司總漕悉改舊法，取數務多，失業逃亡皆由於此。

translations.literal: In recent years the supervisory commissioners and transport directors have all altered the old law, seeking amounts ever greater; loss of livelihood and flight are all due to this.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years supervisors and transport officials have abandoned the old rules and sought ever higher collections—this is why people lose their livelihoods and flee.

sentences.zh: 盍從舊法。」

translations.literal: Why not follow the old law?"
translations.idiomatic: Why not return to the old law?"

sentences.zh: 詔以其言下四川憲司察不如法者。

translations.literal: An edict sent his words down to the Sichuan surveillance commission to investigate those not conforming to law.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Sichuan surveillance commission to investigate officials who violated the old rules.

sentences.zh: 又言：「蜀苦陸運，當諭吳玠，非防秋月，分兵就糧；

translations.literal: He also said: "Shu suffers from overland transport; Wu Jie should be instructed that except when guarding against autumn raids, troops should be divided to draw grain locally;
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Sichuan is burdened by overland supply lines; Wu Jie should be told that except during autumn defense, troops should forage locally;

sentences.zh: 兼選守牧治梁、洋，招集流散，耕鑿就緒，則漕運可省。

translations.literal: and concurrently select prefects and magistrates to govern Liang and Yang, gather the scattered populace, and complete plowing and opening of land—then transport by water route can be reduced.
translations.idiomatic: and appoint good officials in Liang and Yang to gather refugees, restore farming, and then river transport can be cut back.

sentences.zh: 此保蜀之良策也。」

translations.literal: This is the excellent strategy for securing Shu."
translations.idiomatic: This is the soundest way to secure Sichuan."

sentences.zh: 浚去相位，康國乞補外。

translations.literal: When Jun left the chief councilorship, Kangguo begged for an outer appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jun left office, Kangguo asked for a provincial post.

sentences.zh: 趙鼎言于高宗曰：「自張浚罷，蜀士不自安，今留者十餘人，臣恐臺諫以浚故有論列，望陛下察之。」

translations.literal: Zhao Ding said to Gaozong: "Since Zhang Jun was dismissed, scholars of Shu have not felt secure; those who remain number more than ten; your subject fears the remonstrance bureau will criticize them because of Jun and beg Your Majesty to discern this."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ding told Gaozong: "Since Zhang Jun's dismissal, Sichuan officials have been uneasy. More than ten remain at court, and I fear remonstrators will attack them because of Jun—I ask Your Majesty to see this clearly."

sentences.zh: 高宗曰：「朝廷用人，止當論其才與否耳。

translations.literal: Gaozong said: "When the court employs men, one should discuss only whether they have talent or not.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong said: "The court should employ men on talent alone.

sentences.zh: 頃臺諫好以朋黨論士大夫，如罷一宰相，則凡所薦引，不問才否一時罷黜，乃朝廷使之為朋黨，非所以愛人才、厚風俗也。」

translations.literal: Recently the remonstrance bureau likes to discuss scholar-officials in terms of factions; if one chief councilor is dismissed, then all whom he recommended, without asking whether they have talent, are dismissed at once—it is the court that makes them into factions, not the way to cherish talent and enrich custom."
translations.idiomatic: Lately remonstrators love to cry 'faction' at every official. Dismiss one chief councilor and every man he recommended is swept out regardless of merit—the court itself creates factions. That is no way to cherish talent or strengthen public morals."

sentences.zh: 遷右司員外郎，除直顯謨閣、知夔州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, appointed direct attendant at the Xianmo Pavilion, and made prefect of Kuizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, direct attendant at the Xianmo Pavilion, and prefect of Kuizhou.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，起復，撫諭吳玠軍，除都大主管川陝茶馬，卒。

translations.literal: He mourned his mother, was recalled from mourning, pacified and instructed Wu Jie's army, was appointed Grand Commissioner in charge of tea and horses for Sichuan and Shaanxi, and died.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death he was recalled from mourning to reassure Wu Jie's army, appointed Grand Commissioner of tea and horses for Sichuan and Shaanxi, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 論曰：鄧肅、李邴、滕康當危急存亡之秋，皆侃侃正色，知無不言。

translations.literal: The appraisal states: Deng Su, Li Bing, and Teng Kang, in the season of peril when survival hung in the balance, all spoke forthrightly with upright countenance and said whatever they knew must be said.
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal: Deng Su, Li Bing, and Teng Kang, in the hour when the dynasty hung between life and death, all spoke with frank dignity and held nothing back.

sentences.zh: 張守論事明遠，富直柔厄于秦檜、呂頤浩，馮康國說折二凶，皆有用之才也。

translations.literal: Zhang Shou discussed affairs with clarity and far sight; Fu Zhirou suffered under Qin Hui and Lü Yihao; Feng Kangguo persuaded and broke the two villains—all were men of useful talent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shou's counsel was clear and far-sighted; Fu Zhirou was thwarted by Qin Hui and Lü Yihao; Feng Kangguo talked down the two rebels—all men the state could use.
